articles.title: Jaylen Brown Reacts to NBA 2K27 Player Rating in New Video After Trade to 76ers from Celtics
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown had some qualms with 2K after his player rating in NBA 2K27 was revealed.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown had some qualms with 2K after his player rating in NBA 2K27 was revealed.

Brown said he was "offended" that his mid-range rating was only a 90 since he is a "spammer" in that area of the court, and he also questioned how his overall rating dropped two points to 91 after being 93 last year.

It is a bit hard to justify Brown's overall rating going down when he just finished sixth in MVP voting. Even with all of the handwringing over his efficiency, he was the main piece for a Boston Celtics team that won 56 games last season.

Brown will be bringing his 91 overall rating to the Sixers after a surprise trade with Boston in the offseason. He is part of a new-look Philadelphia roster that also added LeBron James to play alongside Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid and VJ Edgecombe.

articles.title: James Harden's Pay Cut, Peyton Watson Recruitment Detailed in New NBA Rumors After Cavs Contract
articles.summary: Veteran guard James Harden was reportedly both flexible and influential during the Cleveland Cavaliers' pursuit of Peyton Watson.
articles.body:
Veteran guard James Harden was reportedly both flexible and influential during the Cleveland Cavaliers' pursuit of Peyton Watson.

In the wake of the Cavs acquiring Watson from the Denver Nuggets this week, ESPN NBA insider Brian Windhorst provided some insight into Harden's role in the process on Friday's episode of Brian Windhorst & The Hoop Collective (beginning at the 12-minute mark) .

"James Harden was willing to opt out of that contract and sit around all summer, and basically pick up the phone whenever the Cavs called and say, 'Yeah, I'll go down a little farther. I'll go down a little farther,'" Windhorst said. "So as the Cavs made various moves, Harden was not only willing to reduce his salary, but he was willing to recruit. He—from what I understand—he recruited Peyton Watson."

The Watson deal was agreed upon Wednesday, as the Cavs sent Max Strus to the Los Angeles Clippers and an unprotected 2031 first-round pick to the Nuggets as part of the three-team trade.

One day later, Harden's agents informed ESPN's Shams Charania that Harden had agreed to a three-year, $97 million contract to return to the Cavaliers.

It was considered a foregone conclusion throughout the offseason that Harden would re-sign with the Cavs, but he waited and allowed the organization to pursue other potential upgrades to the roster.

LeBron James' agent, Rich Paul, confirmed on his Game Over podcast (h/t Conor Smith of the Philadelphia Inquirer ) that the Cavs were among the finalists in the LeBron sweepstakes before he decided to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers.

Had James chosen the Cavs, it would have marked his third stint with the organization he led to a championship in 2016.

Despite LeBron going elsewhere, Harden remained patient, and it paid off in the form of Cleveland adding Watson to the team's already impressive core of Harden, Donovan Mitchell, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Mitchell.

Watson set career highs with 14.6 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.5 three-pointers made per game last season, and adding him to a Cavs team that reached the Eastern Conference Finals last season should make Cleveland an even more serious contender in 2026-27.

articles.title: Marc Stad Buys Majority Stake in T-Wolves, Lynx at $4.5B Valuation in Deal with Marc Lore
articles.summary: Two years after Marc Lore took over as majority owner and governor of the Minnesota Timberwolves, he has sold most of his interest in the NBA franchise as well as the WNBA's Minnesota Lynx.
articles.body:
Two years after Marc Lore took over as majority owner and governor of the Minnesota Timberwolves, he has sold most of his interest in the NBA franchise as well as the WNBA's Minnesota Lynx.

Per ESPN's Shams Charania, Marc Stad will take over as controlling owner of the T-Wolves and Lynx after buying a majority of Lore's interest at a $4.5 billion valuation.

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

MLB legend Alex Rodriguez, who was part of the group that purchased the Timberwolves and Lynx with Lore, issued a statement Friday saying he will be increasing his investment in the team.

"One of the great joys I've had in my career is spending the last few years helping build the Timberwolves and Lynx with my friend and partner Marc Lore," Rodriguez said.

"I'm very excited to announce that this incredible journey reaches a new level today. Marc and Elisa Stad, who have been our partners and friends since we bought the teams, will be increasing their investment and joining me as Co-Chairman. I will also be increasing my investment and spending even more time with the teams as Co-Chairman, Governor of the Lynx, and alternate Governor of the Timberwolves, pending league approval. While Marc Lore will be reducing his role and ownership to focus on his business, he remains an investor and a key part of our partnership. I could not be more energized about this evolution and what we're all going to do together for the Twin Cities."

The Timberwolves sale marks the ninth time an NBA franchise has been sold since 2022, including the deal that saw Lore and Rodriguez purchase Minnesota from Glen Taylor.

It was less than two weeks ago that Mark Walter agreed to sell the Los Angeles Lakers to Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner at a $12.5 billion valuation. Walter's purchase of the franchise had just been approved by the NBA board of governors in October 2025.

Other NBA franchises that have been sold during this period include the Phoenix Suns, Dallas Mavericks, Charlotte Hornets, Boston Celtics and Portland Trail Blazers.

The Lore-Rodriguez purchase of the Timberwolves was officially approved by the NBA in June 2025. Their approval came after a prolonged battle with Taylor, who said in March 2024 that Lore and Rodriguez lost the financial backing needed to make their final payment required to claim majority ownership of the franchise.

Lore and Rodriguez faced questions about their long-term financial ability to maintain a competitive NBA roster. Adrian Wojnarowski, then of ESPN, reported in April 2024 that part of Taylor's concern with selling to them was a budget projection for the 2024-25 season from Lore and Rodriguez that would have cut $27 million in payroll to get under the luxury tax.

In the lone season with Lore and Rodriguez as controlling owners, the Timberwolves had the third-highest payroll in the NBA.

Forbes noted Stad's investment group manages over $35 billion in capital, though his specific net worth is not mentioned in the article.

The Timberwolves have made the playoffs in five consecutive seasons, making the Western Conference Finals in 2024 and 2025. They finished last season as the No. 6 seed in the West and upset the Denver Nuggets in the first round before losing to the San Antonio Spurs in the conference semifinals.

articles.title: NCAA Gets Win In Court On 5-Year Eligibility Rule, But This Is Hardly the End Of the Lawsuits
articles.summary: DENVER (AP) — The NCAA notched an important win in federal court Friday over its much-disputed five-year eligibility rule, though it fell short of shutting down the last-minute shuffling threatening to upend college sports rosters with football season fast approaching.
articles.body:
DENVER (AP) — The NCAA notched an important win in federal court Friday over its much-disputed five-year eligibility rule, though it fell short of shutting down the last-minute shuffling threatening to upend college sports rosters with football season fast approaching.

A 2-1 decision by a panel of the U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals halted, for now, a judge's order that would have granted thousands of athletes an extra season of eligibility. But it did nothing to resolve dozens of other lawsuits and court orders piling up across the country that allow players in the same situation to join teams for the upcoming season.

York Responded to Ad on Prostitution Site Before Arrest

Virtually all these lawsuits involve players who graduated from high school in 2022, whose college eligibility ended last season and who were not included in the NCAA's controversial new rule — less than two months old — that grants most Division I athletes five years of eligibility over five years but doesn't take effect until next season.

"There's a reason we saw so many state-court lawsuits filed" after the now-paused federal court ruling that came down July 31, said Sam Ehrlich, a former lawyer who now works at Boise State and operates the College Sports Litigation Tracker. "It was a 'just in case.' They did it just in case what we just saw happen actually happened."

Among the many athletes watching this unfold and wondering where it winds up are defensive linemen Kellan Wyatt and Stephan Daley, both members of the national championship team at Indiana last season who decided to return after the lower-court decision. So are former Ole Miss starters Dae'Quan Wright, Zxavian Harris and Wydett Williams, who won a ruling from a Louisiana state court giving them another season of eligibility even though they had signed with NFL teams this summer.

While some players hope to land back at their schools, whatever the impact on the rosters, how that works isn't at all clear in many cases. The judge in the case involving the Ole Miss players, for example, gave them a week to enter the transfer portal, which for football players is only open in January.

In appealing the state court cases, the NCAA is expected to invoke parts of Friday's ruling, which agreed with NCAA arguments that it was likely to win the case when it's heard in full — probably several months from now — and that the NCAA would suffer more harm than the players if the court didn't pause the order.

The NCAA can also take heart in an Ohio appeals court that paused a similar injunction involving Xavier basketball Filip Borovicanin and others.

But other than those two cases, Ehrlich said, judges across the country "are unanimous that the NCAA is in the wrong" on the five-year eligibility issue when it comes to the Class of 2022.

Plaintiffs' attorney Rob Shelquist issued a statement calling the appeals court ruling procedural and "not a decision on the merits of the athletes' antitrust claims."

"We are exploring every available option given the split in the panel's ruling and remain committed to fighting for these college athletes whose opportunities and eligibility have been unfairly restricted," he said.

The NCAA's chief legal officer, Scott Bearby, sent a memo to schools telling them they would not be subject to NCAA punishment for allowing any player to compete between the time the July 31 ruling came down and Friday. But he reiterated that those players are no longer eligible.

Bearby also acknowledged that the NCAA would continue to defend lawsuits around the country — a signal that the NCAA knows Friday's ruling offers no guarantees of an end to the roster chaos.

"If anything, I do wonder if there's a part of the NCAA that's, like, 'Maybe we'd have been better off not getting the stay because, boy, there's going to be a lot of lawsuits filed over the next couple of weeks,'" Ehrlich said.

Courts that go beyond filing emergency injunctions and take up the cases in their entirety will have to decide who suffers more harm: Is it players who can't play a fifth year and could lose educational and NIL opportunities? Or incoming freshmen who signed with the idea that they wouldn't be competing against a class of fifth-year seniors?

When the NCAA decided to have the rule kick in next year, it also grappled with that calculation, knowing it couldn't be perfectly fair.

"Fairness is in the eye of the beholder," the NCAA argued in its legal brief in the appeals case. "Countless student-athletes already on campuses, and schools who built their rosters in reliance on the rules the NCAA's membership wrote and agreed to follow, do not believe it is fair for thousands of formerly ineligible athletes to return to competition at the start of the 2026–27 season."

articles.title: Los Wolves cambian de dueño por 4.500 millones de dólares
articles.standfirst: Segunda venta de un equipo de la NBA en menos de un mes
articles.summary: Segunda venta de un equipo de la NBA en menos de un mes
articles.body: El empresario Marc Stad alcanzó un acuerdo para comprar los Minnesota Timberwolves y las Minnesota Lynx por 4.500 millones de dólares, según anunció este viernes la cadena ESPN. Stad, fundador del grupo inversor Dragoneer Investment Group, era hasta la fecha un socio minoritario en ambas franquicias, pero acordó la compra de la participación mayoritaria del empresario Marc Lore. Lore ejercía como copresidente de los dos equipos de la NBA y la WNBA junto con el exjugador de béisbol Álex Rodríguez, quien continuará en su cargo actual. Esta es la segunda venta de una franquicia de la NBA en el último mes, después de que el dueño de Los Ángeles Lakers, Mark Walter, alcanzara el 12 de agosto un acuerdo para vender la franquicia angelina a los empresarios Josh Kushner y Bob Iger por 12.000 millones de dólares. La venta de los Timberwolves y las Lynx es la cuarta operación más alta en la historia de la NBA. Además de la ya mencionada venta de los Lakers a Kushner e Iger, la franquicia angelina pasó a manos de Walter el año pasado tras comprarla por cerca de 10.000 millones de dólares a la familia Buss, propietaria de los angelinos desde 1979. Los eternos rivales del equipo de oro y púrpura, los Boston Celtics, también cambiaron de propietario hace un año a cambio de 6.100 millones de dólares.

articles.title: Los terremotos impiden al Granada jugar en su pabellón
articles.standfirst: Tiene que disputar en Córdoba su primer amistoso ante el Cajasol Coto
articles.summary: Tiene que disputar en Córdoba su primer amistoso ante el Cajasol Coto
articles.body: El enjambre sísmico que sufre Granada ha motivado que no se puedan disputar partidos en el Palacio de los Deportes de la capital al tener que realizarse labores de mantenimiento en sus gradas, por lo que el choque de la Copa Andalucía de la próxima semana entre Covirán Granada y Cajasol Coto Córdoba se jugará finalmente en tierras cordobesas. El Covirán Granada informó este viernes en un comunicado de que, "tras la evaluación realizada" en el Palacio de Deportes granadino "después de la serie de terremotos registrada en la provincia durante los últimos días, se deben llevar a cabo labores de mantenimiento en la grada del recinto". Esto ha llevado a la Federación Andaluza de Baloncesto a trasladar a Córdoba la sede del partido entre el Covirán Granada y el Cajasol Coto Córdoba correspondiente a la Copa de Andalucía y que se iba a disputar la próxima semana en Granada. El club rojinegro ya ha comunicado que "procederá a la devolución del importe de las entradas que ya habían sido adquiridas por los aficionados para el partido". El duelo andaluz se disputará el miércoles a las ocho de la tarde en el Palacio de Deportes Vista Alegre de Córdoba. Los terremotos llevaron al Covirán Granada a suspender sus entrenamientos previstos en las jornadas del martes, el miércoles y el jueves, mientras que el equipo dirigido por Arturo Ruiz ya se ejercita con normalidad desde este viernes pese a que el enjambre sísmico sigue afectando a Granada capital y su área metropolitana con continuos temblores.

articles.title: WNBA Stars Sophie Cunningham, StudBudz, More Reveal What They Bought with Massive New Contracts
articles.summary: WNBA players are enjoying more financial freedom after agreeing to a new collective bargaining agreement in March, and that means treating themselves a little bit even if many are saving and investing.
articles.body:
WNBA players are enjoying more financial freedom after agreeing to a new collective bargaining agreement in March, and that means treating themselves a little bit even if many are saving and investing.

ESPN's Kareem Copeland reported Friday players saw an average increase in pay of 366 percent with their first contracts this season and then relayed what some of them said they bought with their new money.

Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham purchased a VRBO in Arizona and explained she plans on expanding that business plan.

"I'm about to probably buy one in Nashville and Florida, and so I'm just starting to make a business outside of the court," Cunningham said. "It's good, it's fun. I'm trying to buy places that I want to go visit, so when I'm there, I don't have to pay for it.

"I think it's a long time coming, but now you have to be smart with that money. You can't just go out and blow it all or not invest. I think it allows all of us to kind of grow and be businesswomen."

Others took a different approach, including Minnesota Lynx guard Courtney Williams.

"I went to the strip club and blew a bag," Williams said. "No, I'm being dead serious. Like, that particular strip club will never see me for the rest of my life. Like, I did too much in there.

"Man, they probably know me by my name."

Williams and Seattle Storm guard Natisha Hiedeman are collectively known as "StudBudz," and the latter bought Williams a customized, seven-foot statue of the anime character Goku for her birthday.

"I ain't gonna lie, I spent a little bit on that," Hiedeman said. "They had to make it, ship it, do everything.

"She been saying she wanted one ... and she's putting her little crib together. But we said we're done buying each other expensive gifts now. So, that was her last gift from me."

Elsewhere, Washington Mystics forward Kiki Iriafen bought a black Porsche Cayenne coupe, Indiana Fever guard Lexie Hull bought a Tesla and Atlanta Dream forward Rhyne Howard bought a new Louis Vuitton bag.

"I definitely saved a lot of my money, invested a lot of money," Iriafen said. "I finally did my 401[k] this year. I did not do that last year, so I was really proud of myself for doing that.

That seemed to be a theme with many of the players investing but also enjoying a splurge, which is not surprising after they worked so hard during negotiations for the new CBA.

articles.title: Otro recital de España para meterse en la gran final
articles.standfirst: La selección femenina sub 16 luchará por el oro este sábado (19.30) ante Eslovenia
articles.summary: La selección femenina sub 16 luchará por el oro este sábado (19.30) ante Eslovenia
articles.body: La selección española femenina sub 16 ya está en la final del Eurobasket. Era lo más probable dado el camino que había seguido hasta la semifinal. Tras cinco partidos llegaba al duelo ante Letonia con una media de anotación de 110,8 puntos y cinco triunfos por una ventaja media de 79,2. Un abuso en toda regla de un equipo que borda el baloncesto. Aunque Letonia fue el rival que más complicaciones dio al combinado que entrena Madelen Urieta, las bálticas también cayeron con cierto estrépito en una semifinal dominada por España (91-53). Un resultado que vuelve a sorprender y deja clara la calidad del equipo de España femenino sub 16. Letonia tenía claro el plan. No dejar a España correr y parar su ritmo con faltas. De hecho en el primer cuarto más igualado que ha jugado el combinado español (15-14), las de Urrieta fueron 20 veces a la línea de personal, fallando 11 de esos tiros. Además España tuvo problemas desde el triple, 0/9 iniciado el segundo cuarto. Pero la igualdad se acabó dos minutos después de comenzar el segundo acto. A 8:42 para el final Letonia se puso por delante, 15-16... y el partido se acabó. De ahí al final del cuarto España engrasó su maquinaria, mejoró la defensa y corrió, para arrollar a su rival. Un primer parcial de 12-0 que luego fue de 23-2 (38-18) abría de par en par la puerta de la final para España. Al descanso se llegó con 46-22 que dejaba el partido casi liquidado. España no bajó su ritmo en la reanudación elevando su ventaja sobre un equipo letón que se acabó entregando a la superioridad española. Amelia Alonso acabó con un doble-doble (16 puntos y 10 rebotes), Paula Reynal hizo 15+8, Aisha Mbengue aportó 12 pntos y Anastasia Lishchuk logró un 9+8. España buscará el oro, que sería el segundo consecutivo y el duodécimo en total, este sábado a partir de las 19.30 ante Eslovenia que se cargó a Francia en la otra semifinal, 58-67. En ese partido la pintura tendrá una batalla de apeliidos ilustres con Anastasia, hija de Sergei Lishchuk, ante Ema, hija de Erazem Lorbek.

articles.title: 76ers Reportedly Land New Assistant Coach Who Won 2 NBA Titles with LeBron James
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers are finalizing a deal with veteran coach Phil Handy to serve as an assistant under head coach Nick Nurse, according to Andscape's Marc J. Spears.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers are finalizing a deal with veteran coach Phil Handy to serve as an assistant under head coach Nick Nurse, according to Andscape's Marc J. Spears .

Handy will reunite with the newly-signed LeBron James. Handy was among James' assistant coaches with the Cleveland Cavaliers from 2015 to 2018, and the Los Angeles Lakers from 2019 to 2024.

Most recently, Handy was head coach of Mist BC in the women's three-on-three Unrivaled basketball league in 2025, and he was an assistant coach with the Dallas Mavericks last season.

Jayson Tatum's dad blunt about Celtics roster

During his two stints as one of James' coaches, the 54-year-old Handy won a pair of NBA championships, doing so with the Cavs in 2016 and the Lakers in 2020.

In between, Handy spent the 2018-19 season as an assistant with the Toronto Raptors, helping coach them to their first and only championship in franchise history.

The head coach during Handy's one-year tenure in Toronto was Nurse, so Handy's arrival in Philly will serve as a reunion for them as well.

It has been a busy offseason for the Sixers, as they reshaped their roster by acquiring five-time All-Star Jaylen Brown for Paul George and draft picks in a trade with the Boston Celtics before signing James in free agency.

James, 41, is preparing to enter his record 24th NBA season, and he chose to sign with the 76ers with an eye toward winning a fifth career title.

The Sixers' projected starting five of James, Brown, Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid and VJ Edgecombe is arguably the best in the league, plus they have some quality bench pieces in Anfernee Simons, Dean Wade, Dominick Barlow and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, and a championship-winning head coach in Nurse.

Handy gives the 76ers even more championship experience, aiding them in their pursuit of their first NBA title since 1983.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark 'Wouldn't Mind Seeing' Taylor Swift Wear Nike Caitlin 1 Signature Shoe
articles.summary: Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark could be hoping her past hangouts with Taylor Swift will lead to the pop star endorsing her new signature Nike shoe.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark could be hoping her past hangouts with Taylor Swift will lead to the pop star endorsing her new signature Nike shoe.

When asked in a recent Q&A by SLAM 's Jared Ebanks what celebrities she would like to see wearing the Nike Caitlin 1, Clark answered, "I wouldn't mind seeing Taylor Swift in a couple versions that I think she would probably like."

"Other than that, I honestly think it's really cool just seeing other WNBA players or other NBA players wear your shoe," Clark added. "I think that's really special. So, I'll definitely be trying to get as many college hoopers, NBA hoopers, WNBA hoopers."

The Nike Caitlin 1 is set to debut Oct. 1 in the "Racer Blue" colorway, which is one of more than 10 colorways Clark has teased ahead of the shoe's release.

Clark was spotted sitting next to Swift as the singer's now-husband Travis Kelce played for the Kansas City Chiefs game last October.

The Fever star later said in a January appearance on Kelce's New Heights podcast she "definitely" had interest in making a Chiefs colorway or player edition of the Nike Caitlin 1.

"Maybe we can get Andy Reid to coach in them at some point," Clark told Travis and Jason Kelce.

Clark has already gotten some celebrity endorsement ahead of the Nike Caitlin 1's release. She shared a photo earlier this offseason of Travis Scott trying on the shoes in an all-black colorway.

articles.title: DeMar DeRozan, Nuggets Reportedly Agree to Contract After Peyton Watson Trade, Updated Salary Cap
articles.summary: After two years with the Sacramento Kings, DeMar DeRozan has found a new home.
articles.body:
After two years with the Sacramento Kings, DeMar DeRozan has found a new home.

The veteran will reportedly sign a new contract with the Denver Nuggets, per Chris Haynes of NBA on Prime. The one-year deal will be worth $3.9 million per Shams Charania of ESPN.

Heat still have 2 rosters spot left after signing Klay

This move continues a tight salary cap crunch for the Nuggets.

They were already $1.3 million over the second apron before the deal, per Bobby Marks of ESPN.

The Kings waived DeRozan and the remainder of his expiring contract on July 6. DeRozan would have counted for $25.7 million against the cap had he stayed in Sacramento.

As soon as DeRozan hit free agency, it was clear a number of contenders were going to try to get him on their roster. After the Nuggets traded Peyton Watson to the Cleveland Cavaliers, their focus reportedly shifted to DeRozan.

While DeRozan is 36 years old, he's remained consistent as he's gotten older. Last year, he put up 18.4 points, 4.1 assists and 2.9 rebounds per game while starting 77 contests. He's also avoided injury throughout his career and has played 70 or more games in each of the last five seasons.

He might not have the same athleticism and explosiveness that he had in his youth, but he should be able to serve as a valuable option alongside Nikola Jokić and Jamal Murray.

The signing also gives DeRozan the chance to play for a contender rather than the Kings, who are likely on their way to another rough season. Whether the 2026-27 campaign will see DeRozan win his first title remains to be seen.

The Nuggets didn't have a huge budget to work with this offseason, but picking up DeRozan is a valuable signing that could be the difference for them this postseason.

articles.title: Jonathan Kuminga Updated Landing Spots After Klay Thompson, DeMar DeRozan Contracts
articles.summary: The market for free agent forward Jonathan Kuminga might have become clearer now that Klay Thompson and DeMar DeRozan have reportedly landed with their next teams.
articles.body:
The market for free agent forward Jonathan Kuminga might have become clearer now that Klay Thompson and DeMar DeRozan have reportedly landed with their next teams.

The Minnesota Timberwolves and Los Angeles Lakers remain top potential landing spots for Kuminga after Thompson and DeRozan reportedly committed to the Miami Heat and Denver Nuggets, respectively.

Kuminga is currently an unrestricted free agent after the Atlanta Hawks declined his team option. NBA insiders Marc Stein and Jake Fischer previously reported the Hawks are expected to be "pretty choosy" with any potential sign-and-trade scenarios involving Kuminga.

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

ESPN's Shams Charania reported Friday the Miami Heat are expected to sign Thompson after he clears waivers following a buyout by the Dallas Mavericks.

That will put the Heat on track to use most of the team's remaining midlevel exception to sign Thompson, per the Miami Herald 's Barry Jackson and Anthony Chiang.

NBA insider Chris Haynes reported later the same day the Denver Nuggets are signing DeRozan.

Some other potential landing spots for Kuminga had already taken themselves out of the running with acquisitions earlier this offseason.

The Cleveland Cavaliers approached the first luxury tax apron by signing Peyton Watson and James Harden, while the Hawks spent the offseason adding former Oklahoma City Thunder players Aaron Wiggins and Lu Dort.

The Timberwolves remain a potential landing spot for Kuminga, in whom HoopsHype's Michael Scotto recently reported the team had "expressed interest" after missing out on signing LeBron James.

The Wolves have "their starting power forward spot up for grabs and their $6.06 million taxpayer mid-level exception available for the taking," Scotto noted.

The Athletic's Dan Woike previously reported the Lakers had expressed interest in Kuminga, but that as of July "momentum has stalled with the sides far apart on terms and L.A. not overly motivated to push significant draft capital into sign-and-trade scenarios."

Woike noted Kuminga "could re-emerge as a target if his market remains tepid."

ESPN's Brian Windhorst said in Friday's episode of The Hoop Collective podcast he feels there is "still a window" for the Lakers to complete a sign-and-trade deal featuring Kuminga and Lakers guard Jaden Hardy.

With the final NBA roster spots filling up, teams have about two months left to complete any late offseason moves before Opening Day rosters are finalized Oct. 19.

articles.title: España saca buena nota en su examen contra Nigeria
articles.standfirst: Gana con claridad a las campeonas de África en un segundo tiempo arrollador
articles.summary: Gana con claridad a las campeonas de África en un segundo tiempo arrollador
articles.body: Aunque a España le faltan las cinco jugadoras de la WNBA, la preparación va dando pasos muy sólidos hacia lo que quiere Miguel Méndez: un equipo sin fisuras muy reconocible que crezca desde la defensa. Ante Nigeria mostró dos caras, una más frágil ante el planteamiento físico de las africanas, que duró algo menos de 20 minutos y otra, con una enorme mejoría defeniva y con vocación de correr. La segunda versión le valió el trunfo ante Nigeria (83-58) en el torneo internacional de Tenerife. Las campeonas africanas (lo son en las últimas cinco ediciones), asustaron al principio. Llegaron a tener cierta ventaja, 26-34 a falta de 3:17 para el final del segundo cuarto, y se fueron con 36-40 al decanso. Ese paso por vestuarios le sentó mucho mejor a España. Seguramente Méndez incidió en la defensa para empezar a construir el ataque y sus jugadoras lo interpretaron a la perfección. El partido cambió por completo, Nigeria anotó tan sólo nueve puntos en el tercer acto mientras que España, dominando el rebote, empezó a correr y a encontrar mayor efectividad en el tiro. Andrea Vilaró anotó cuatro triples, Iyana Martín tres y Mariona Ortiz, dos. La ventaja de España fue creciendo hasta los 25 puntos finales que fue la mayor ventaja de la selección. El parcial tras el descanso fue de 47-18 para las de Méndez en una muestra de hacia dónde fueron capaces de llevar el choque. El colapso nigeriano fue total ante un equipo que se había convertido en un vendaval. España acabó liderada en puntos por Iyana Martín (12), seguida por Helena Pueyo (11) y Mariona Ortiz (10). Destacaron también los siete rebotes de Irati Etxarri, que fue una de las jugadores que impregnaron de defensa el juego de la selección. La mejor anotadora del partido fue la nigeriana Macaulay (18). articles.title: Top NBA Free Agency Landing Spots For Jalen Duren and Jonathan Kuminga
articles.summary: It's late August, and only a few scraps remain on the NBA free-agent market. The odd quirk this offseason: The top two players left are big names.
articles.body:
It's late August, and only a few scraps remain on the NBA free-agent market. The odd quirk this offseason: The top two players left are big names.

Jalen Duren is coming off an All-NBA season. Jonathan Kuminga is still just 23 years old.

Both could make a major difference wherever they land.

Let's check in on the best places for them to play in 2026-27.

Even if the relationship feels increasingly strained by the ongoing restricted free agency stalemate, Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons are still each other's best fit.

Duren may not be the All-NBA force he resembled during the 2025-26 regular season, but he's also better than the guy who so conspicuously flopped in the playoffs. The Pistons can't easily replace him, and even if they're right to play hardball on Duren's next deal, they should still try to avoid the riskier outcomes of a qualifying offer or a sign-and-trade.

If the Pistons get too worried about Duren accepting the qualifying offer and want to address their secondary creation needs, a sign-and-trade deal with the Clippers that returns point guard Darius Garland might be worth exploring.

Duren would give the Clippers a scoring threat, rebounder and roll man to pair with rookie guard Keaton Wagler.

Another playmaking sign-and-trade option: Sending Duren to the Houston Rockets for Alperen Sengün. The mechanics would be tricky (just as they would for LA), but Duren would work well with the existing young core of Reed Sheppard, Amen Thompson and Jabari Smith Jr.

Jonathan Kuminga would have been a strong theoretical fit next to James Harden, Donovan Mitchell, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen. But after the Cavaliers' trade for Peyton Watson, reporting points to the Los Angeles Lakers and Minnesota Timberwolves as the top two favorites.

Kuminga's athleticism and foul-drawing abilities should make him attractive to both teams, as well as the Milwaukee Bucks, with Milwaukee having more reason to chase a high-risk prospect. After failing to meet expectations in both Golden State and Atlanta, it's starting to seem that Kuminga's struggles are more about his style of play than any system suppressing his talent.

While the Lakers are reportedly interested and could use a high-upside option like him on the wing, they have more to lose if things don't pan out.

articles.title: Ranking Top 2026 NBA Free Agents Still Available After James Harden Re-Signs with Cavaliers
articles.summary: The 2026 free-agent period has seen a whirlwind of action, with multiple stars changing teams and available players flying off the board.
articles.body:
The 2026 free-agent period has seen a whirlwind of action, with multiple stars changing teams and available players flying off the board.

LeBron Watch 4.0 concluded July 24 when The King said he'd be joining the 76ers. Jaylen Brown is joining James in Philadelphia, while Kawhi Leonard is headed back to Toronto. And that's just scratching the surface of the market.

On the free-agent front, Walker Kessler is headed to the Lakers in a sign-and-trade, as L.A. made a flurry of moves. And now we know that James Harden is re-signing with the Cleveland Cavaliers on a three-year, $97 million deal.

With all that action said and done, who's left on the board?

The following is a descending ranking, with the top free agents listed at the bottom.

Team: Atlanta Hawks 2025-26 Salary: $11.5 million Rights: Full

Vincent is an experienced veteran guard, with a strong playoff resume with the Miami Heat. He spent the last few years with the Los Angeles Lakers as an occasional starter, but was sent to the Atlanta Hawks before the trade deadline.

While he shot a steady 36.9 percent from three-point range for the Lakers, the fit wasn't seamless in Atlanta, where he dropped to 30 percent.

In the right situation, Vincent should be able to help a team that needs veteran bench leadership. At this stage in his career, he may not get more than a minimum contract.

Team: LA Clippers 2025-26 Salary: $5.6 million Rights: Early Bird

The Clippers have several questions this offseason. The James Harden and Ivica Zubac trades suggest the franchise is going younger, with players like Darius Garland, restricted free agent Bennedict Mathurin and the No. 5 pick from the Indiana Pacers via the Zubac deal.

Batum is similar to Al Horford. They're seasoned veterans past their primes, but still elite in basketball intelligence with the knack for hitting clutch open shots.

The Clippers declined Batum's $5.9 million team option, per B/R's Jake Fischer , giving them greater cap flexibility and the chance to give his spot to a younger player, but he still holds value in this league for postseason contenders.

Team: Denver Nuggets 2025-26 Salary: $3.1 million Rights: Non-Bird

Fit in the NBA can be everything, and Brown fits in Denver. He helped the team win a championship in 2022-23, shooting the second-best three-point percentage in his career (38.5). Returning as a free agent on a minimum contract, Brown is at his best at 38.1 percent from deep.

Not that he takes too many attempts. He knows his role is to play defense, feed off Jokić, and do whatever is needed to get his squad a win. While he's only on a one-year deal, Brown may return to Denver, given his success with the Nuggets.

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

Team: Chicago Bulls 2025-26 Salary: $5 million Rights: Full

The Bulls picked up Richards from the Phoenix Suns via trade ahead of the deadline, desperate for a starting-capable center. Through 20 games, Richards has thrown his weight around as a physical, old-school big man, averaging 9.4 points and 7.6 rebounds.

Richards may be best as a backup center, but he can fill that starting role for teams in need. Chicago may keep him to play behind Nicolas Claxton, who will be joining the Bulls in trade in early July.

ESPN is reporting the Atlanta Hawks are declining Jonathan Kuminga's $24.3 million team option, making him a free agent.

Last season, the Golden State Warriors finally traded Kuminga after a lengthy, uncomfortable couple of years. The 23-year-old forward didn't fit with coach Steve Kerr's philosophy. The Hawks took a flier on Kuminga‚ and he enjoyed a late postseason surge against the New York Knicks, but Atlanta didn't see enough value at the $24M price tag.

Team: LA Clippers 2025-26 Salary: $9.2 million Rights: Full (restricted)

The Indiana Pacers, committed to avoiding the luxury tax as much as possible, chose to trade Mathurin to fill a void at the center position (adding Ivica Zubac in the deal). The Clippers have had an eye on Mathurin for some time, as they need more young, talented players.

Mathurin has found a friendly home with the Clippers. Through 28 games with the Pacers, he averaged 17.8 points a game (37.2 percent from three). With the Clippers, he contributed 17.4 per game (though he's still searching for his three-point shot).

Despite his age, 23, Mathurin has NBA Finals experience, scoring 27 points in Game 3 against the champion Oklahoma City Thunder.

Team: Detroit Pistons 2025-26 Salary: $6.5 million Rights: Full (restricted)

Along with MVP candidate Cade Cunningham, Duren has emerged over the last two years as a true game-changer in Detroit. He's grown on both sides of the floor, especially defensively on a very stingy Pistons squad.

Named to the All-NBA Third Team and a first-time All-Star, Duren averaged a career high of 19.5 points a game for the best team in the Eastern Conference by record (60-22). He was up and down throughout the playoffs, but Duren should get a sizable raise to stay. If the Pistons aren't willing to max him out, the Lakers have plenty of cap room for an offer sheet.

Cam Thomas was recently let go by the Brooklyn Nets and Milwaukee Bucks. Jaden Ivey was also waived by the Chicago Bulls. Ben Simmons never found a home during the 2025-26 season.

Others include Brandon Williams, Ochai Agbaji and Aaron Holiday.

articles.title: El Barça anuncia el décimo fichaje de su nuevo proyecto: Yoan Makoundou
articles.standfirst: El ala-pívot francés tiene 26 años, mide 2,07 y ficha hasta 2028
articles.summary: El ala-pívot francés tiene 26 años, mide 2,07 y ficha hasta 2028
articles.body: El Barça ha anunciado este sábado la contratación del ala-pívot Yoan Makoundou hasta el 30 de junio de 2028, por lo que el jugador francés se convierte en el décimo fichaje del renovado proyecto azulgrana que dirige el esloveno Aleksander Sekulic. El versátil jugador francés, de 26 años y 2,07 metros, llega procedente del AS Monaco, tras formarse en el Cholet Basket, y cuenta con experiencia en la Euroliga. Durante su trayectoria, Makoundou también ha jugado cedido en el Buducnost Podgorica y el Turk Telekom Ankara, mientras que la pasada temporada disputó un breve período con los Fujian Sturgeons, de la liga china. Se trata de un interior que puede jugar en diferentes posiciones, con mucha energía y capacidad atlética, y que, según el comunicado de la entidad, es una incorporación "de presente y de futuro". Makoundou ya estuvo en el radar del club azulgrana en el mercado de verano de la temporada 2025-26, pero la operación finalmente no fructificó. Debutó en la LNB francesa en la temporada 2019/20 con el Cholet, aunque el salto definitivo a la élite llegó la temporada siguiente, con buenos registros en la competición doméstica y, sobre todo, en la Liga de Campeones de la FIBA, donde registró una media de 10,4 puntos, 5,2 rebotes, 13,4 de valoración en los 5 partidos que disputó. En la temporada 2021/22. se consolidó, con una mejora en el tiro exterior -pasó de un 27 a un 34,5% desde la línea de tres- y unas estadísticas interesantes de media en la LNB, con 10,2 puntos, 5,4 rebotes y 12,5 de valoración en 33 partidos de fase regular. Su progresión le permitió debutar con la selección francesa absoluta, con la que disputó 13 partidos en diferentes ventanas de clasificación para el Mundial del 2023 y el Eurobasket de 2025. En la temporada 2022-23, Makoundou fichó por el Mónaco con el que jugó sus primeros ocho partidos en la Euroliga, además de gozar de protagonismo en la liga francesa. En los dos siguientes cursos, encadenó dos cesiones al Budcnost Podgorica (2023-24) montenegrino y al Turk Telekom Ankara turco (2024-25). Con el equipo balcánico, registró una media de 11 puntos, 4,6 rebotes, 12,6 de valoración de media en la Eurocopa y se convirtió en una pieza clave para conseguir el título nacional gracias a sus aportación (con 12,8 puntos, 5 rebotes) en los 'play-off'. En el Turk Telekom, promedió 11,2 puntos, 4,9 rebotes y 12,4 de valoración en la Eurocopa, mientras que en los 'play-off' por el título de la liga turca alcanzó los 11,3 puntos y 5 rebotes de media. El curso pasado jugó en las filas del Mónaco, aunque a mediados de temporada rescindió el contrato y firmó por los Fujian Sturgeons de la liga china, donde en 19 partidos anotó 15,2 puntos y capturó 6,2 rebotes de media. Tras su experiencia asiática, el Mónaco recuperó al jugador parisino para disputar los 'play-off' por el título con unos registros notables de 11 puntos y 3,6 rebotes. Makoundou es la décima incorporación del Barça para la temporada 2026-27 tras los fichajes de los bases Justin Robinson y Umoja Gibsol, el escolta Agustín Ubal, los aleros Stanley Umude y Tyrese Martin, los ala-pívots Tosan Evbuomwan y Olivier Nkamhoua, y los pívots Olek Balcerowski y Josh Nebo. La dirección deportiva capitaneada por Xevi Pujol trabaja en cerrar la plantilla con la incorporación de un último jugador interior.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark, Fever Clinch 2026 WNBA Playoff Berth, Updated Bracket Picture and Standings
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever are going to the playoffs for a third straight year.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever are going to the playoffs for a third straight year.

Indiana clinched a postseason spot with the Portland Fire's 82-79 loss to the Toronto Tempo on Friday night.

Following the clinching, Indiana is in fourth place in the WNBA standings and playoff picture:

The fourth seed will play the fifth seed in the first round of the WNBA playoff bracket, which means the Fever are currently slotted into a matchup against the Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream.

There are only two games separating the Golden State Valkyries as the No. 2 seed and Dream in the fifth spot, so plenty of things can change over the final month of the regular season.

The WNBA is preparing to take a three week hiatus after Aug. 28 for the FIBA World Cup before play resumes on Sept. 18.

While a championship is the end goal for the Fever, they are surely focused on remaining healthy in the playoffs as well. After all, they reached the WNBA semifinals last season despite Clark, Sophie Cunningham, Sydney Colson and Aari McDonald all being sidelined with injuries.

Indiana defeated the Atlanta Dream in the first round and pushed the Las Vegas Aces to overtime in the decisive fifth game of the second round. Considering Las Vegas went on to win the championship, it was quite the effort from the shorthanded Fever.

Ideally for Clark and Co., they will be much healthier as they pursue the title this time around.

Everything in Indiana starts with the Big Three of Clark, Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston, which gives the team enough offensive firepower and versatility to play with and defeat even the best opponents in the league come playoff time.

All three of them made the All-Star Game this season and are averaging a combined 63.3 points per game. While role players such as Cunningham, Monique Billings and Lexie Hull provide some depth, the entire offense runs through the trio.

Clark is one of the faces of the league and a dominant scorer and facilitator who opens up looks for everyone else because of the defensive attention she draws. Mitchell has taken advantage of that more than anybody and is the team's leading scorer with an arsenal that includes three-point shooting and the ability to finish through contact as she drives the lane.

As for Boston, she is a double-double threat every time she steps on the floor and someone who provides important interior defense to take some of the pressure off Clark and Mitchell.

That lets Clark and Mitchell provide even more scoring, and they did so in record-setting fashion this season:

If the guard duo that represents one of the best one-two punches in the league continues to pour in the points and Boston continues to dominate on the inside, the ceiling for a healthy Fever team that is now heading to the postseason is the WNBA title.

Bronny James doesn't have any strong takes about his father leaving the Los Angeles Lakers to join the Philadelphia 76ers this offseason.

When a fan asked Bronny about LeBron James signing with the Sixers, the Lakers guard had a simple response: "It's whatever, it's my dad."

Bronny and LeBron played two seasons together in Los Angeles. They became the first father-son duo to appear in the same NBA game when Bronny made his debut against the Minnesota Timberwolves on Oct. 22, 2024.

Overall, the James duo shared the court for 294 minutes over the past two years. Their last appearance together as teammates was Game 3 of the Western Conference semifinals against the Oklahoma City Thunder on May 9.

The Lakers' season ended the next game, leading to LeBron ending his eight-year tenure with the club. He went on to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Sixers in free agency.

Bronny is entering year three with the Lakers. He showed improvement from his rookie campaign in limited playing time with 2.9 points on 40.9 percent shooting and 1.2 assists per game in 42 appearances last season.

The first time Bronny and LeBron might meet as opponents is on Christmas Day when the Sixers visit Crypto.com Arena to take on the Lakers.

articles.title: Los Nuggets fichan a DeRozan para crear un nuevo 'Big Three'
articles.standfirst: El equipo de Colorado contará con el talento de DeMar durante la próxima temporada
articles.summary: El equipo de Colorado contará con el talento de DeMar durante la próxima temporada
articles.body: Lo de los 'Big Three', aquella fórmula que, aunque usada muchos años antes, se puso de moda cuando LeBron James se fue a Miami para juntarse con Chris Bosh y Dwyane Wade, sigue en boga en la NBA. Hace unos años sólo unos pocos tenían el privilegio de contar con uno, ahora casi todos los equipos lo tienen. Los Nuggets ya tienen el suyo. Mientras Nikola Jokic se divierte jugando partidos FIBA con Serbia, Denver trata de construir un equipo contendiente al título no sea que el riesgo de que su estrella quiera marcharse crezca cada año más. Tras el frustrante traspaso de Peyton Watson a Cleveland por las necesidades del límite salarial, la reacción de los de Colorado ha sido sonada: DeMar DeRozan. Es cambiar futuro (Watson, 24 años) por presente (DeRozan, 37), pero los Nuggets quieren pelear por el anillo esta misma temporada y por ello se han fijado en un anotador puro con una extraordinaria experiencia en la NBA y con una probada durabilidad. A pesar de sus 37 años y de que comenzará su temporada 17, DeRozan es un jugador habitual en los partidos, poco propenso a los problemas físicos. De hecho estuvo en 77 de los 82 partidos que jugó su equipo la pasada temporada y ha disputado al menos 70 partidos en las cinco últimas campañas. Pero sobre todo es un anotador puro capaz de producir 18,4 puntos por noche con cerca del 50% de acierto. Justo antes de la campaña recién terminada había encadenado al menos 20 puntos de media en 12 temporadas. DeRozan firma por una temporada y 3,9 millones de dólares. Es una simbiosis, el jugador llega a un equipo necesitado de talento, y el equipo recibe a un jugador que quiere ganar un anillo, que aún no tiene. DeRozan habló durante la pretemporada con los Miami Heat, los Washington Wizards y los New Orleans Pelicans. Estuvo cerca de los primeros a los que incluso se le vinculó tras una reunión con Ban Adebayo, pero los Heat pusieron su radar más cerca de Klay Thompson, al que han terminado por convencer. Acuciados por el límite salarial, los Kings cortaron a DeRozan a principios de la pretemporada y este se convirtió en agente libre. Ahora llega a un equipo en el que tiene qye mezclar con Jamal Murray y Nikola Jokic. Precisamente cada movimiento de los Nuggets se hace pensando en el serbio y esos rumores de que si el equipo no lucha por estar arriba y ganar un título, podría demandar un traspaso. Los Nuggets saben que 'el Joker' aún tiene al menos un anillo potencial en sus manos y quieren lograrlo rodeándole de experiencia y talento. Y en ese aspecto, DeRozan cumple con todas las exigencias.

articles.title: Breanna Stewart Wants a Safe Space as Transgender Debate Sparks Rallies at Fever Games
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — New York Liberty star Breanna Stewart has always seen the WNBA as an inclusive place that has served as a safe space for both its fans and the players. That's been challenged lately.
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — New York Liberty star Breanna Stewart has always seen the WNBA as an inclusive place that has served as a safe space for both its fans and the players. That's been challenged lately.

The WNBA has been the subject of recent debates on whether transgender women — people assigned male at birth who transition to align with their gender identity — should be allowed to participate in the league. There has never been such a player in the WNBA. Although the league's collective bargaining agreement says the WNBA is restricted to women, it contains no more specific language about gender identity or sex assigned at birth.

No Cunningham-Carrington Issues in Rematch (AP)

There have been small rallies and protests outside Indiana Fever games after the issue came to a head when Sophie Cunningham of the Fever said in an ESPN profile published last month that she was opposed to transgender girls and women competing in girls' and women's sports. There were a pair of peaceful rallies representing both sides of the transgender issue that took place before the Fever faced the New York Liberty on Saturday night.

"Knowing that rallies are happening on both sides shows the platform that the W has and the stunts for attention are just continuing to try and ride the wave that we have," Stewart told a small group of reporters Saturday morning. "I want Liberty fans and even Indy fans that are going to come here tonight to be able to have this arena be a safe space."

Cunningham felt that all the attention that her comments have garnered has been positive by bringing more fans to the game.

"You have a lot of new fans, not only just watching, but coming to games and seeing the environment and seeing the talent," she said before the game. "I think anytime you can get more eyes on the W, that's an awesome thing, because then that inspires other young kids that maybe have never seen the game or heard about the game or been to a game, they get that experience. So I definitely think that it's been a very positive thing."

At least three fans were asked by WNBA security personnel to cover shirts that had messages about transgender women participating in women's sports during last Sunday's game at Atlanta between the Dream and the Fever. The league later said the fans should have been free to wear those shirts.

Stewart said Liberty fans specifically, but WNBA fans in general, come to games because "they can feel like they can be themselves in whatever capacity that is and we don't want to lose sight of that."

The Liberty forward said everyone is entitled to their own opinion and if that stops being allowed there are much bigger issues. However, she said, trying to divide teams and players shouldn't be tolerated.

"If we don't allow (free speech), we need to like really kind of go back and look at more things. I think the bigger thing is people are trying to divide us as teams, but also as teammates or as opponents," she said. "This league is incredibly inclusive and what we continue to fight for and stand up against. So, we don't want to take that platform away."

Stewart has been an ally for the transgender community during her career. She faced some online backlash last year when one of her signature shoes had a Harry Potter theme to it. Stewart is a huge fan of the Harry Potter books and subsequent movies by author J.K. Rowlings, who has drawn criticism for her anti-trans stance.

Stewart has donated royalties from that shoe to The Trevor Project, a suicide prevention and crisis intervention nonprofit organization for LGBTQ+ youth.

articles.title: New NBA Rumors Reveal Klay Thompson Gave Up Huge Money on Mavs Contract to Land with Heat
articles.summary: Klay Thompson reportedly sacrificed $9.8 million of his 2026-27 salary to secure a buyout from the Dallas Mavericks, according to Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.
articles.body:
Klay Thompson reportedly sacrificed $9.8 million of his 2026-27 salary to secure a buyout from the Dallas Mavericks, according to Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.

Per multiple reports , Thompson is planning to sign a two-year, $13 million deal with the Miami Heat to join Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo following his divorce from the Mavs.

Thompson changing addresses makes sense, even if the financial cost to do so was fairly steep.

The Heat desperately needed more shooting on the perimeter, and while the 36-year-old Thompson is no longer one of the league's elite 3-and-D wings, he still averaged 11.7 points and shot 38.3 percent from three in 69 games for the Mavericks last season.

Miami could utilize him in a sixth-man role behind a starting five of Giannis, Adebayo, Davion Mitchell, Tim Hardaway Jr. and Andrew Wiggins. Or Thompson could start with Hardaway coming off the bench. Either way, the depth chart thins out considerably after that, and players like Bobby Portis and either Thompson or Hardaway will have considerable roles off the bench.

The Mavericks, meanwhile, are rebuilding around a younger roster, headlined by second-year star Cooper Flagg. Thompson's buyout will allow the Mavericks to give more minutes to younger, ascending talents.

"Klay is one of the great players and competitors of his generation, and we are grateful for everything he brought to the Mavericks organization," Mavericks president of basketball operations Masai Ujiri said in a statement . "We have tremendous respect for Klay and all that he has accomplished throughout his career, and we wish him nothing but the best moving forward."

articles.title: BIG3 League Championship 2026 Winner, Prize Money, Highlights, Box Score and Top Player Stats
articles.summary: The 2026 BIG3 league came to an exhilarating conclusion on Saturday as the Boston Ball Hogs defeated Dallas Power in the title game behind a game-winner from Jeremy Pargo.
articles.body:
The 2026 BIG3 league came to an exhilarating conclusion on Saturday as the Boston Ball Hogs defeated Dallas Power in the title game behind a game-winner from Jeremy Pargo.

The Ball Hogs entered the matchup as 3.5-point underdogs, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , but pulled off an upset with an incredible performance from its starters.

Jayson Tatum's dad blunt about Celtics roster

In its ninth season since being founded by Ice Cube and Jeff Kwatinetz in 2017, eight teams battled for the prize money.

Last season, it was announced that "the two winning teams coming out of the Week 9 playoffs will be awarded the $1 million win bonus," in addition to their regular-season salaries, according to BIG3's Hannah Palacios .

The Ball Hogs went 6-3 during the season behind co-captains Garlon Green and Deshawn Stephens, wrapping it all up with their first championship, led by an MVP performance from Pargo.

The Power finished a dominant season behind co-captains Cameron Smith and Glen Rice Jr., going 8-1.

Despite an impressive season and a standout championship performance from Elijah Stewart, who scored 19 points, they could not get it done in the final game.

Former Georgetown University big man Greg Monroe got things started in the 2026 championship game with a tough bucket under the rim before the two teams began their back-and-forth battle for the lead heading into halftime.

The Ball Hogs held a narrow two-point lead at halftime, with Green, Pargo and Stephens accounting for all of their points.

The race to 50 points came down to the wire, with Power within three points of the target and eyeing their second championship while the Ball Hogs were stuck at 43.

Boston's Pargo launched a 4-pointer to tie the game at 47-all, refusing to roll over as both teams eyed a 3-pointer to win it.

After an and-one put Monroe at the free-throw line with a chance to put the game away, he missed the opportunity, and Boston's Pargo called game with a 4-pointer to clinch the comeback victory and secure Boston's first-ever championship.

articles.title: España gana el oro y culmina un Europeo perfecto
articles.standfirst: Gana en la final a Eslovenia 40-87, en otro choque decidido antes de llegar al descano
articles.summary: Gana en la final a Eslovenia 40-87, en otro choque decidido antes de llegar al descano
articles.body: España cerró otro extraordinario verano en las categorías de formación. La Federación española de baloncesto, ejemplo absoluto en el mundo, vuelve a recoger una cosecha brillantísima con medallas en seis de los siete campeonatos en los que ha participado. Sólo en el Europeo masculino sub 20 (cuartos) no se tocó metal, y destacan la plata del Mundial sub 17, el oro del femenio sub 18, y los bronces del masculino sub 20 y sub 16 y el femenino sub 16. Pero la útima, la lograda por las selección sub 16 femenina, es colosal. Un oro de dominio absoluto en un campeonato perfecto. La selección, que ganó la final a Eslovenia 40-87, acabó con una media de anotación de 104,5 por partido por tan sólo 35,8 en contra, ganando partidos incluso por más de 100 puntos. Quizá desde los tiempos de tiranía de los equipos de la URSS, no se veía algo así. Y esto ha sido incluso superior. Un dato que corrobora esto es que si los partidos del torneo se hubieran disputado sólo con el primer y segundo cuarto, España hubiera ganado el oro igualmente. En los siete partidos que disputó, la selección de Madelen Urieta llegó al descanso con 20 o más puntos de diferencia, es decir, decidiendo los partidos en apenas 20 minutos. Sus segundas partes fueron casi un trámite. Eso pasó también contra Eslovenia, a la que España ya ganaba con enorme claridad cuando ambos equipos enfilaban el túnel de vestuarios (19-39). Para el choque, las premisas de Urieta eran que España fuera España, que jugara con ritmo, que corriera y que abusara de la pintura. Y que defendiera, pero sobre todo el perímetro. Con superiordad interior, lo que España quiso es evitar que las eslovenas se metieran en el partido desde el triple, que tantos réditos les dio en las semifinales ante Francia. La misión fue perfecta y las balcánicas acabaron anotando su primer (y único) triple a un minuto del final del tercer cuarto y con todo decidido. Tras un primer cuarto demoledor, 9-21, en el que España provocó 11 pédidas del rival, el segundo acto sólo mostró más defensa española y más superioridad interior. En ese aspecto, asusta pensar la progresión que pueden llegar a tener Amelia Alonso, jugadora fabulosa por calidad e instinto y Anastasia Lishchuk, dominante a lo largo de todo el campeonato siendo sub 14. También ha brillado mucho, en un bloque en el que sobresalir es complicado, Paula Reynal. Para el final del tercer cuarto, las de Arieta ya rondaban los 30 de diferencia, 32-61, una ventaja que fue creciendo durante el último cuarto, convertido ya en una fiesta española en la ciudad rumana de PItesti. El +47 final representa la mayor paliza en una final en la historia del campeonato, superando los 25 puntos logrados por la URSS ante Bulgaria (72-67, 1984), la URSS ante la República Checa (83-58, 1987) y Rusia de nuevo ante la República Checa (72-47, 2014). Paula Reynal fue la mejor anotadora de la final con sus 18 puntos. Acabó como la líder en anotación de un equipo sensacional. Por detrás de ella en la final, Sara Fernandez de Cuevas aportó 13 puntos, Blessing Ajisebutu hizo 12 y Amelia Alonso, tremendo su rendimiento en los dos aro, acabó con 9 puntos y 8 rebotes. La medalla ganada en Rumanía es la duodécima de oro para España y la vigésima en total. La selección lidera el medallero con esos 12 oros por los 8 que ganó la URSS. Eslovenia repite la plata que logró el pasado año perdiendo precisamente contra España.

images.caption: España levanta la copa de campeonas de Europa sub 16. FIBA PHOTO.

Kimberly Kanayan N'Simba /Francia), Amelia Alonso y Paula Reynal (España), Nadine Graudina (Letonia) y Veronika Ferjancic (Eslovenia), formaron el quinteo ideal del torneo. Alonso fue la MVP. FIBA PHOTO.

articles.title: VJ Edgecombe Talks Role on New-Look 76ers After LeBron James Signing, Jaylen Brown Trade
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers are going to have to iron out their roles after the offseason additions of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, among others.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers are going to have to iron out their roles after the offseason additions of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, among others.

But as teams try to deal with stopping those two alongside Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey, second-year standout VJ Edgecombe is expecting to see plenty of open looks.

"It's fine if they don't respect me, I'll just get a bunch of open shots," he told reporters regarding opposing teams if they leave him unguarded. "I'm just working. That's the main thing for me. That comes with work. Whatever I want I got to work for it. I'm willing to do that."

For Edgecombe, the main thing remains winning a championship.

"I mean, it don't matter what happens, there's always going to be someone that has something to say," he said. "But I just want to win. I'm going to still be aggressive, still be myself. If that comes with less shots or more shots, who knows. I don't know how the course of the game is going to go. I'm just excited to play alongside my teammates. I think we have a chance to do something really special."

Because Embiid has a long injury history and because James is 41, both players will need their minutes and appearances managed carefully during the regular season. That should mean plenty of games where one, if not both, are sidelined, which would mean a greater role for Edgecombe in those contests.

He certainly looked like a star-in-the-making during his rookie season, averaging 16.0 points, 5.6 rebounds, 4.2 assists and 1.4 steals while shooting 35.4 percent from three. His future is bright, even if the Sixers need him to take on a more complementary role next season.

articles.title: Mark Mitchell Commits to Kentucky in Transfer Portal, Former 5-Star Also Played for Duke, Missouri
articles.summary: Forward Mark Mitchell will indeed be staying in college after a temporary injunction granted him a fifth season of college eligibility.
articles.body:
Forward Mark Mitchell will indeed be staying in college after a temporary injunction granted him a fifth season of college eligibility.

According to On3's Joe Tipton , Mitchell will be joining the Kentucky Wildcats in the transfer portal.

Mitchell went through the NBA draft process and signed an Exhibit-10 contract with the Denver Nuggets, having exhausted his eligibility last season. But new NCAA rules this offseason allow players up to five years of eligibility within a five-year period, though Mitchell's class wasn't included in that ruling.

In response, Mitchell joined a lawsuit contesting his lack of eligibility. He and the other players in the case were granted a temporary injunction by Jefferson County Circuit Court Judge Brian Edwards.

Similar rulings elsewhere have cast a lot of uncertainty regarding eligibility and the transfer portal across the college football and basketball landscape:

Mitchell's addition would be a pretty huge one for Kentucky. The former Duke and Missouri forward averaged 18.3 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.6 assists for the Tigers last season, shooting 54.7 percent from the field and 38.8 percent from three.

Mark Pope hit the transfer portal hard, landing the No. 1 class in that regard. That helped cover for a more modest year in recruiting and followed the recent trend of more veteran-laden squads winning the national championship. Mitchell would further improve Kentucky's chances.

Much depends on the NCAA's response to the various court rulings impacting the sport, but for now, Kentucky has landed a major contributor for next season.
