Sabrina Ionescu and the New York Liberty won a high-scoring affair against Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and the Indiana Fever on Saturday night.

The Liberty, who were a 1.5-point favorite at FanDuel Sportsbook, held on for a 108-102 victory.

Ionescu was one of four Liberty starters in double figures. She scored 12 points, while Breanna Stewart had 22 and Leonie Fiebich produced 20.

Ionescu added four assists and three rebounds to her 12-point outing.

Clark was one of three Fever players to score over 20 points in the defeat.

The Fever star had 11 rebounds and assists to go along with her 21 points and pair of three-pointers.

Cunningham was the only bench player on either side to reach double digits with 10 points.

The Fever played from behind for a majority of the second half and could not complete a comeback on the road.

New York moved to 23-15 with the victory, while Indiana dropped to 24-14. The two teams are now just a game apart in the multi-team race for the No. 2 seed.

articles.title: Bold Predictions for Every NBA Team's Best New Weapon
articles.summary: The 2026 NBA offseason delivered external additions to all 30 rosters.
articles.body:
The 2026 NBA offseason delivered external additions to all 30 rosters.

We'll be just as generous by extending a bold prediction around the best new weapon on all of those franchises.

Before starting, it's worth noting what a bold prediction is and is not. It is an optimistic (but still realistic) look at what could happen if everything breaks right. It is not, however, leaning into the absurdity for the purpose of doing so.

Accuracy is still the overall objective, even if the application of it looks a bit rosier than normal. These may not all be things that we think will happen, but they are things we can envision with some best-case-scenario kind of good fortune.

Bold prediction: Dort makes an All-Defensive team

Some will question the boldness of this prediction, which is fair given that Dort was an All-Defensive first-teamer in 2024-25. That said, he just finished his seventh season in the NBA, and that stands as the lone All-Defensive selection of his career.

He must be at his most powerful and most disruptive best to earn a second honor. Being cast away by the Oklahoma City Thunder—where he started for a championship team just two seasons back—might maximize his motivation. Plus, Atlanta should be filthy on defense with chaos-creators like Dort, Dyson Daniels and Nickeil Alexander-Walker all around the wings.

Bold prediction: George averages 20-plus points

The Jaylen Brown-less Celtics have a standing need for a new Jayson Tatum co-star. George might be most comfortable filling that role, even if Derrick White and Payton Pritchard have big advantages when it comes to institutional knowledge.

But White and Pritchard have always handled support roles; George has legitimate experience in the spotlight. And as a superstar's sidekick, a role he handled alongside Russell Westbrook in Oklahoma City and with Kawhi Leonard in L.A. George's scoring volume has dialed down in recent seasons (hence the boldness of this prediction for a career 20.5 points per game scorer), but shifting back into a more prominent offensive role than the one he had in Philadelphia should reverse that trend.

Bold prediction: Brown will lead rookie rotation regulars in assist-to-turnover ratio

Shrewd decision-making isn't the first thing that comes to mind with Brown, who plays a flashy, risk-reward style. But if he had more scoring help than he did at Louisville or with the summer league Nets, he would be better able to pick his spots. And the creative passes he throws and prowess in pick-and-roll plays suggests there are some pretty awesome quarterbacking skills at play.

It would still be pretty stunning to see Brown paces rotational rookies in assist-to-turnover ratio after averaging 4.7 assists against 3.1 giveaways in college (and 4.0 against 2.7 this summer). But that feels like a reasonable (if optimistic) wager on his developmental growth and ability to maximize an offense featuring a couple of proven high-end scorers in Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr.

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

Bold prediction: Reid averages a 20-point, 10-rebound double-double

Reid arrives in Buzz City as, objectively speaking, the best backup big man in basketball. The Hornets clearly see an even brighter future in front of him. He was by far the most significant player they received for their stunning subtraction of franchise face LaMelo Ball.

The Hornets will feature Reid in ways to help justify that change-of-direction to fans still on the fence about it. And if he's getting 30-plus minutes on the regular—he'll be featured at both the 4 and 5 spots—he should be a double-double machine. To this point, his career per-36-minutes averages sit at 19.7 points and 8.5 rebounds.

Bold prediction: Wilson will win Rookie of the Year

There are certainly bolder R.O.Y. candidates than the draft's No. 4 pick, but it's not like Wilson is the favorite for the award. He doesn't have the polish of Cameron Boozer, the shotmaking of Darryn Peterson or the scoring bag of AJ Dybantsa. And if defensive playmaking is Wilson's greatest strength right now, that's not exactly a trait that traditionally wins over award-voters.

So, why even bother making this prediction? Because Wilson has the right blend of explosive athleticism, competitive fire and unwavering confidence that makes you want to believe. He also appears primed for success with this roster. His transition scoring should perk up alongside a pass-first point guard like Josh Giddey, Wilson's defensive activity should be emboldened by the interior protection provided by Nic Claxton and Norm Powell's scoring support should keep Wilson from having to force the issue, which could be big for his shooting rates.

Bold prediction: Watson tallies 150-plus three-pointers

The Cavs are convinced that Watson will be the one who finally stops their revolving door at small forward. Well, that or they at least deemed him the most capable of doing that among wings they could afford to acquire and pay.

Either way, they're now fully pot-committed to the fifth-year swingman, losing access to both tradeable first-round picks and tradeable mid-sized salaries. Opponents will do everything they can to challenge the wisdom of this commitment by packing the paint against Cleveland's bigs and crowding their guards. Watson should get a ton of open looks from three, and he could use all of these chances to nearly double the career-high 81 threes he made last season.

Bold prediction: Johnson plays the fewest minutes—by a wide margin—of the top 10 picks

In theory, Johnson shouldn't be hurting for playing time. He is joining a team that just lost 56 games and has all of its present and future hopes wrapped around a 19-year-old (Cooper Flagg). You'd think opportunities would be abundant, especially since Dallas took Johnson, the No. 9 pick, earlier than expected.

In reality, Johnson is set to join a crowded frontcourt that may not have an obvious place for him right now. Daniel Gafford and Dereck Lively II are still manning the middle. The forward spots are overloaded with established vets, like PJ Washington, Naji Marshall and Santi Aldama, plus a few developmental priorities, like Flagg and 2024 No. 1 pick Zaccharie Risacher. Dallas won't completely forget about Johnson, but it will find it difficult to give him major minutes, especially if his outside shooting doesn't dramatically outperform expectations.

Bold prediction: DeRozan averages the fewest points since his rookie season

It took the Nuggets until the latter half of August to make their first splash of the offseason. And even then, it's been several seasons since the signing of DeRozan would qualify as anything close to a canonball. It speaks to Denver's lack of depth—which feels unforgivable with this club being the league's lone resident in the second apron—that getting the 37-year-old version of DeRozan feels like a pretty big deal.

In some ways, it sort of is, because this bench unit was begging for buckets, and DeRozan can provide them in bunches. That said, the Nuggets can only afford to find him so many minutes, because defense was a pressing concern even before his arrival. Something around 15 points per outing feels reasonable and would be his lowest scoring output since he was an NBA first-timer back in 2009-10.

Bold prediction: Collins averages at least two three-pointers

A 28-year-old veteran like Collins feels pretty well cemented into a career by now. You wouldn't look for major changes in his statistical profile, because his stat lines generally feel like they've been churned out by the same assembly line. Save for a half-season spike on a brutally bad 2024-25 Utah Jazz team, his production hasn't deviated much over the past six seasons.

After signing with the Pistons, though, one number seems set to spike—well beyond where it's ever been before. That would be Collins' three-point makes, which have never gone above 1.5 per game and sit at 1.1 for his career. Detroit will need a lot more than that, though, both to offset the spacing constraints of their other frontcourt spots and to keep Collins as a viable offensive threat when he presumably may not have as many chances to hammer home some finishes as a pick-and-roll screener if Jalen Duren ever re-signs.

Bold prediction: Lendeborg lands on the All-Rookie first team

Is this low-hanging fruit? You could maybe call it that. Lendeborg is pretty well-regarded, and he doesn't have to elevate too far from this summer's No. 11 pick to the upcoming season's All-Rookie first team.

Still, history holds a lot of cautionary tales for prospects who are this old (23) and drafted this high very well. Lendeborg would need to be a norm-breaker, in other words, and do so while handling the spotlight run-off from teaming with Stephen Curry, plus the roster uncertainty of having several key players working their way back from injury and the front office being forever on the lookout for trade-market upgrades.

Bold prediction: Bogdanović logs 1,500-plus minutes

Financially speaking, the Rockets aren't beholden to Bogdanović, who needed just a one-year, minimum deal to come to Houston. The 34-year-old has recently battled both injury issues and general ineffectiveness, so it's a low-cost flier that may never amount to much.

Except for the fact that, basketball speaking, Houston kinda really needs a lot of what Bogdanović does. Spacing is a pressing concern, and he's a career 38.1 percent three-point shooter. Playmaking is another, especially if Fred VanVleet looks rusty after a season lost to ACL recovery, and Bogdanović has long been a reliable secondary table-setter. If his body holds up, he could wind up filling a much larger role than anticipated.

Bold prediction: Oubre is a Sixth Man of the Year finalist

If you listed the many reasons for Pacers fans to feel optimistic for this upcoming season, it'd take a little while before you got around to their signing of Oubre. He is a solid option, he's just not as big of a talking point as, say, the return of Tyrese Haliburton or the full integration of Ivica Zubac.

But Oubre should fill a prominent role in this rotation. And he just might fill it awfully well, since his athleticism, downhill scoring and ignitable outside shots should all be system fits for an offense that operated at a top-10 pace the last time a healthy Haliburton was behind the wheel.

Bold prediction: Wagler won't make an All-Rookie team

No, this is not an overreaction to Wagler's shaky showing on the summer circuit. It does, however, share some of the same athletic concerns that contributed to those aesthetically unpleasing exhibitions.

"Wagler's struggles might keep me up at night...if I were his employer," The Athletic's John Hollinger wrote in July. "He scored at a high rate but not very efficiently and made almost no impact across the rest of the box score. In particular, he struggled with ball pressure and was invisble defensively."

To be fair to Wagler, summer league never felt like the right environment for his cerebral, one-step-ahead play style. That said, his physical struggles were predictable given his athletic limitations, and those challenges will only grow more difficult against actual NBA defenders. He needs time to adapt his body and his approach, not to mention things could be wonky at first figuring out his fit alongside Darius Garland.

Bold prediction: Kessler splashes 80-plus three-pointers

The Lakers had reasons for aggressively pursuing—and paying a premium for—Kessler this offseason, and his outside shooting almost certainly wasn't one of them. Still, they should allow him to dabble from distance, since he has experimented with an outside shot since his days at Auburn and finally saw some proof of concept during the previous campaign.

Granted, the sample size was tiny, but he still got off to a hot start by hitting 6-of-8 three-pointers over the five games he played. If he can be even a semi-viable threat from deep, then this offense will be that much harder to handle. And it pretty much needs to be top-notch given the rather glaring defensive concerns with this roster construction.

Bold prediction: Boozer scores 1,000-plus points, shoots 50-plus percent

Given the sky-high expectations tied to Boozer, this year's No. 3 pick, those numbers probably don't jump off your screen. For an NBA rookie, though, they definitely should. Only 45 freshman have ever hit both marks, and all but nine of them debuted before the 2000s.

This would not at all be normal for a rookie, in other words, but Boozer doesn't look normal. He is polished beyond his years and has a seasoned veteran's feel for the game. Even as a potential focal point in Memphis, he won't force bad shots and will make full use of his wide-reaching skill tree.

Bold prediction: Antetokounmpo will be an MVP finalist

The boldness here needs context, because a healthy Antetokounmpo is almost perpetually locked into a top-three finish in MVP voting. Still, predicting him to land even higher would seem reckless when Nikola Jokić, Victor Wembanyama and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander all exist.

Those players could all have better team-success arguments than Antetokounmpo, too, as the depth of the Eastern Conference (and Miami's lack of depth after its blockbuster buy) could force the Heat into their fifth consecutive Play-In appearance. Antetokounmpo would have to be individually awesome to overcome that and still be a top-three MVP candidate, but our crystal ball can't wait to see all the fun ways Erik Spoelstra will use his new superstar.

Bold prediction: Herro will earn his second All-Star selection

Between incoming stars (LeBron James, seemingly Kawhi Leonard) and those returning from injury (Tyrese Haliburton, Jayson Tatum in a way), the bar for what's required to be an Eastern Conference All-Star has clearly elevated. A motivated Herro still has a chance to clear it.

Herro's return to his home state of Milwaukee offers a "fresh start for everyone," as he told The Athletic's Eric Nehm . It should also be an open invitation for Herro to feast on offensive opportunities buffet-style. His volume could be in line for a sizable boost, and he is a good enough shooter to maintain respectable conversion rates.

Bold prediction: Ball averages three times more assists than turnovers

There are a million and one unknowns for Ball's first go-round in the Gopher State and a million and one ways in which things could go very right or horribly wrong. Even in a bold world, it would be precarious to try to make sense of all of these uncertainties.

But here's one thing that is known: Ball is no longer atop of the offensive hierarchy. He is a true second option to Minnesota's megastar Anthony Edwards and should operate accordingly. That means less forcing the issue and more selectively picking his spots. It also means there should be more threatening weapons on the receiving end of Ball's passes, which, when paired with his vision, should allow him to record the first 3-to-1 assist-to-turnover ratio of his career.

Bold prediction: Watford scores 500 points

A sleepy summer for the Pelicans almost excluded them from this exercise and certainly gives Watford a by-default feel for his best-weapon status. He might not even hold it for long since his $2.4 million salary is only partially guaranteed .

Given New Orleans' injury history, though, and the quiet nature of this front office, Watford has a decent chance to stick around for the whole season. Even if the plan is to keep him behind emergency glass, there's a good chance that glass will be broken often enough for the sixth-year swingman to clear the 500-point threshold for the first time.

Bold prediction: Drummond will average 15 points and 15 rebounds per 36 minutes

Don't be fooled by New York's minimal investment in Drummond; the Knicks really need this to work. With Mitchell Robinson in Boston, and Ariel Hukporti off to Philadelphia, the backup big man plans for the 'Bockers start and stop with Drummond.

He needs to be more of an innings-eater, too. He has to be hyperactive on the glass and reliable around the rim on both ends. With this projected role and the support he'll have around him, he could be in line for his best per-36-minutes marks since 2023-24.

Bold prediction: Mara isn't a rotation player until 2027, still ranks top three among rookies in blocks

Despite making multiple financially motivated cuts to the roster, the Thunder don't have an obvious place to put Mara right now. Which might be just as well, since he hardly appeared rotation-ready at Summer League.

Once he gets settled, though, he might find OKC's depth chart fairly easy to climb at center. The size and shot-blocking he can provide just aren't a part of Jaylin Williams' arsenal. And who knows how much Thomas Sorber will play? An optimistic read on Mara would have him cracking the rotation in January or February—just in time for the 7'3" paint protector to compile a top-three block total among rookies.

Bold prediction: Vučević shoots 40-plus percent from three

Vučević's second tour of duty with Orlando will look nothing like the first. He used to be a centerpiece; now, he'll be an ancillary source of size, strength and spacing on the second unit.

That will torpedo his volume production—he averaged just 9.7 points in 21.1 minutes after his deadline move to Boston—but it could be a big boon for his efficiency. Playing off the likes of Paolo Banchero, Desmond Bane and Franz Wagner will allow Vučević to be much more selective, perhaps setting the stage for only the third 40-plus three-point percentage of his career.

Bold prediction: Brown averages his fewest points since 2019-20

Brown arrives in Philadelphia fresh off the most productive campaign of his career. And he clearly enjoyed his time in the mostly Jayson Tatum-less spotlight last season, which he described as his "favorite" multiple times this summer. Still, his numbers are about to come way down with the star-laden Sixers, and he sounds fine with that.

"My focus is winning," Brown said at his introductory presser. "...How do we win night in and night out? Sometimes it may look different. Whatever it takes. At this point in my career, nothing else really moves me."

Hopefully, he means what he said, because the ball won't find him nearly as often in Philly. He is going from a two-star system in Boston to now sharing the floor with LeBron James, Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey. (Not to mention 2025-26 Rookie of the Year finalist VJ Edgecombe.) Calling for fewer than 20 points per game would still feel like a slight toward Brown, but he may not have the touches to land far above that.

Bold prediction: Bridges is the Suns' second-highest scorer

There are big fans of Bridges in Phoenix. Maybe his alma mater helped with that, or perhaps this was as simple as the Suns noticing a hole at power forward and a need for more scoring power. Either way, they saw enough in him to be willing to sacrifice two key rotation players (Grayson Allen and Royce O'Neale) and an unprotected 2023 first-round pick to pry Bridges out of Buzz City.

Bridges' best skill is volume scoring, so look for Phoenix to give him chances to provide as much of that as he possibly can. Bridges may not be the most efficient scorer around, but he could definitely be more efficient than the other leading candidates for this gig (Jalen Green and Dillon Brooks).

Bold prediction: Morant paces Portland's point guards in minutes

Of all the predictions made here, this might veer the closest to being reckless. Morant has played 79 games the past three seasons combined. Expecting any kind of consistency from him is asking a lot, especially given the inherent challenges of Portland's overcrowded backcourt.

Then again, he is only 27 years old, so you'd love to think there's a chance he can put his injury issues behind him. And he did look pretty great right before being shut down last season (21.8 points and 8.8 assists over his final eight outings). So, maybe things can fall in his favor. He can't be any bigger of an availability risk than Damian Lillard (a 36-year-old returning from an Achilles tear), and Morant's track record is clearly richer than Scoot Henderson's. If Jrue Holiday suits up elsewhere (he could see more time at the 2 and 3), this could happen.

Bold prediction: Acuff is a R.O.Y. finalist

Summer league was largely an eyesore for Acuff, who left a barrage of bricks and little separation between his assists and turnovers in Las Vegas. The Kings may have already forgotten and forgiven those struggles, if only because they so desperately need him to carry into whatever comes next for the organization.

Trades involving Domantas Sabonis, Zach LaVine and Malik Monk are long overdue. The young core developing behind those vets has some intrigue, but lacks star power. Everything is aligned for Acuff to be among the rookie leaders in points and assists, and if he ranks highly in both categories, then he'll be among the last three standing in the Rookie of the Year race.

Bold prediction: Harris is top-five on the team in clutch minutes

The Spurs just won 62 games and reached the NBA Finals. Nearly every member of their rotation is still ascending. It would be tricky for any newcomer to make a meaningful dent in the rotation, but San Antonio sought out Harris for a reason.

Is that reason big enough to lock Harris into the closing lineup? That would lead to some uncomfortable omissions—probably two of Devin Vassell, Julian Champagnie and Dylan Harper—but Harris' blend of shooting, off-the-dribble creation and experience could force the issue.

Bold prediction: Graves makes an All-Rookie team

Blame the snag in the Kawhi Leonard trade talks for denying us the chance to make a much more significant bold prediction, but at least Graves is a fascinating rookie. It isn't often that a freshman reserve at Santa Clara becomes a top-20 pick, but here we are.

Graves' athletic limitations are worrisome, and his path to major playing time is tricky to plot with the forward glut in Toronto. Still, the skill versatility and IQ are major selling points—and things that have worked for a lot of other lanky forwards in this organization. It might be a slow burn just as it was with Collin Murray-Boyles last season, but Graves could similarly emerge as a crucial piece of the rotation and an All-Rookie performer by season's end.

Bold prediction: Peterson outscores his new backcourt mate

Between Peterson's arrival as the No. 2 pick, and Keyonte George's ascension as one of the 2025-26 season's breakout stars, Utah's backcourt appears in tremendous shape. The Jazz should have a wealth of scoring and playmaking production from their new perimeter pairing, perhaps providing the perfect counterbalance for the Lauri Markkanen-Jaren Jackson Jr. tandem up front.

While Peterson and George will be working alongside one another, this prediction pits them against one another and tasks Peterson with clearing a pretty high bar, as George averaged 23.6 points last season. Even amid the outburst, though, he never generated the kind of hype Peterson already has, and the rookie should have ample opportunities to live up to it as both an on-ball three-level scorer and off-ball shotmaker.

Bold prediction: Dybantsa leads a postseason charge in Washington

OK, maybe this is more a team prediction than an individual one, but it was hard to think of a bold prediction for Dybantsa. Locking the No. 1 pick into a R.O.Y. finish would've been too obvious. Calling for an All-Star spot would've been reckless.

So, let's instead pair this prediction of a smooth transition for Dybantsa with a wild ride up the East standings for Washington. Few teams have a youth collection this deep and compelling, let alone two legitimate stars to lead it (Trae Young and Anthony Davis). This conference looks as competitive as ever, but the Wizards can at least wiggle their way into the top 10 with Dybantsa playing a primary role in that ascension.

The Atlanta Dream extended their WNBA playoff streak to four seasons.

Atlanta is assured of a top-eight position with a 99-89 win over the Phoenix Mercury. Angel Reese scored a career-high 31 points and hauled in 14 rebounds for her 26th double-double of the season.

By this point, simply qualifying for the postseason doesn't count as success for the Dream. They didn't make it out of the first round in any of their last three trips, and they've won just one playoff game since 2018.

Especially with the core of the squad largely remaining for the last few years, Atlanta can't afford to keep hitting the same ceiling when it counts.

There might be some concern within the fanbase that that's exactly what will happen again this fall when it feels as though we've seen this story before.

Allisha Gray, Rhyne Howard and Reese were all All-Stars, but none of the three has taken a huge leap on the court.

Howard is averaging 18.2 points per game, which is close to her scoring average between 2023-25 (17.4 points). Gray is a good offensive engine who's setting a career high with 19.4 points, but her three-point shooting (32.5 percent) has gone backwards. Reese is still a walking double-double (16.3 points, 12.0 rebounds), yet the same concerns about her inefficiency and lack of range remain.

Adding further worry for Atlanta is that some of the supporting players aren't matching the heights they enjoyed in 2025.

Sixth Player of the Year Naz Hillmon has regressed as a floor-spacer. Guard Te-Hina Paopao was shooting just 34.4 percent overall before she was sidelined by a right leg injury. Four-time All-Star Brionna Jones hasn't looked as sharp since suffering a torn meniscus while playing overseas.

It's not as though the sky is falling for the Dream. They rank third in net rating (plus-6.8), per WNBA.com , but it's impossible not to contrast their performance now with that of a season ago, when they tied for the league's second-best record (30-14) and were second in net rating (plus-9.3).

Reese is a big wild card too because she didn't make the playoffs in her two years with the Chicago Sky. She's unproven on that stage, and her limited range is the kind of thing an opposing team will try to target in a postseason series.

At their best, the Dream can compete with just about any other team in the league, but few will have them as Finals favorites. Should they fail to turn a corner, general manager Dan Padover may need to take a long, hard look at the roster construction.

articles.title: Angel Reese Has Career Night, Final Box Score Stats, Highlights as Dream Clinch Playoffs vs. Mercury
articles.summary: Angel Reese enjoyed a career night as the Atlanta Dream sealed their place in the WNBA playoffs.
articles.body:
Angel Reese enjoyed a career night as the Atlanta Dream sealed their place in the WNBA playoffs.

The third-year forward had 31 points in a 99-89 win over the Phoenix Mercury on Saturday. She posted her 26th double-double of the season thanks to grabbing 14 rebounds.

"I think she keeps getting better and keeps being able to expand her game," Dream coach Karl Smesko said, per ESPN.com . "I think she really found her opportunities to be physical. They weren't really sending doubles, so she had her opportunities to catch the ball in the short and do some post moves to score. She was able to get behind on some ball screens for some layups where our guards were able to find her, got a couple of putbacks.

"She was scoring in a multitude of ways, had a really great fourth quarter for us, and it's good to see her have one of her best games of her career, offensively."

Reese did a lot of damage around the basket, taking full advantage of Phoenix's lack of depth in the frontcourt. Only three of her points came from the charity stripe.

The three-time All-Star has made a conscious effort to widen her range, though it remains a work in progress.

Reese's 50 three-point attempts are more than double her previous high (22), but she's shooting just 18 percent from deep. Her overall efficiency hasn't improved, either, as she's knocking down 47.3 percent of her two-pointers, nearly equal to her 2025 output (47.8 percent).

The postseason figures to be a major test for Reese and the Dream as a whole. She didn't taste playoff basketball during her two years with the Chicago Sky, while Atlanta is coming off a disappointing first-round exit a season ago.

Games often slow down in the playoffs, and spacing the floor becomes more imperative. Players such as Reese, who aren't reliable three-point threats, can be exploited by opposing coaches.

Assuming she doesn't suddenly blossom into a stretch 4 over the next month, Reese may nonetheless remain effective through her rebounding and relentless motor in the paint.

The Dream, meanwhile, are clearly looking to her to provide something they were lacking when they got bounced by the Indiana Fever.

articles.title: Everything Caitlin Clark, Stephanie White Said After Fever's Loss to Breanna Stewart, Liberty
articles.summary: Indiana Fever coach Stephanie White wants to see more consistency from her squad following a 109-102 loss to the New York Liberty on Saturday.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever coach Stephanie White wants to see more consistency from her squad following a 109-102 loss to the New York Liberty on Saturday.

"I thought that there were some moments where we made them uncomfortable. Not enough," White told reporters in her post-game press conference. "When we were up into the ball pressuring, I thought we got some really good things on the defensive end. And then there were lapses, lapses that caused fouls that went to free throws. Lapses that allowed offensive rebounds. Lapses that allowed soft switches into cuts. Lapses on the offensive end where we didn't move the ball. We didn't find the right play, didn't find the right pass."

No Cunningham-Carrington Issues in Rematch (AP)

White cited how the Fever shot 57.1 percent overall and went 11-of-26 on three-pointers, yet came out on the losing end.

"More than anything, I think this is just an opportunity for us to keep learning how much of a sense of urgency you have to play with every single possession," she said. "This is playoff basketball right now and there has to be an urgency every single possession."

The Fever are in the fourth leg of a five-game road trip, which got underway on Aug. 16. Star Caitlin Clark didn't want to use the schedule as an excuse for the team's showing against New York.

"Yeah our schedule's tough — I think we play more back-to-backs than just about anybody in the league," she said. "But it is what it is. … Everybody's tired. Everybody's sore. Who cares? Figure out a way to make yourself feel better and suit up and go play."

Clark finished with 21 points, four rebounds and seven assists. She was one of three Fever players to score 20-plus points, joining Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston. Mitchell added to her WNBA record by doing it for the 22nd straight game.

"I think it says what a high level that she's playing at," White said of the dynamic guard. "I think it shows how difficult it is to guard her one-on-one. I think the biggest thing for me is how she's doing it in a lot of different ways. You used to play Kelsey a lot to just get downhill. You would play her for the spot-up. I think her ability to play off two feet, to get to the free-throw line, to read the game in a number of ways has been really impressive. It's tough to do what she's been doing night in and night out."

Looking ahead, Clark put a positive spin on Indiana's difficult stretch by pointing out the team can quickly rebound on Sunday against the Chicago Sky before it has a few days off to recover.

The Fever have clinched a playoff berth but will want to improve their position in the WNBA standings. At 24-14, they're in fifth and only trail the second-place Golden State Valkyries by three games.

Getting into fourth would mean having home-court advantage in the best-of-three first round, and climbing to third would allow Indy to avoid the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx in the semifinals.

In general, the Fever have looked better since the WNBA All-Star break but have some areas in which they need to sharpen up over the final month.

While Philadelphia 76ers legend Julius Erving believes the team improved this offseason, he's not immediately crowning them NBA champions.

Erving told TMZ Sports he gave the Sixers a "thumbs up" for the Jaylen Brown trade, adding they will be "one of the most talented teams." The Hall of Famer does, however, have some questions about a lineup that includes 41-year-old LeBron James and 21-year-old VJ Edgecombe.

"There's a big age discrepancy between the youngest, you know, which is VJ, and LeBron," he said. "So how that works, it remains to be seen."

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

Erving compared the roster to experimenting with a new dish in the kitchen you've never tried.

"You're trying to create something special. You're trying to create something," he said. "You go in the kitchen and you mix the ingredients, and then once you put fire under there, you see whether it's going to be good, great, or OK."

Erving's assessment probably represents the general consensus on Philadelphia.

On paper, a starting five of James, Brown, Edgecombe, Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey is the best in the NBA. Getting all of the pieces to fit together could be tricky, though, when four of the five are accustomed to working on the ball.

Philly is also hedging a lot of its hopes on Embiid staying healthy, which is a familiar concern. The team's ceiling changes if he's not on the floor because there's a steep drop between he and backup center Adem Bona.

The Sixers have the talent to challenge the New York Knicks for the Eastern Conference crown. Still, NBA superteams haven't fared well in recent years, so it won't be a complete shock if the experiment proves to be a bust.

articles.title: Jokic vuelve a superar a 'Wemby', pero Serbia cae sobre la bocina
articles.standfirst: Jaylen Hoard anota la canasta ganadora gala a pesar de la remontada de 19 puntos de los serbios
articles.summary: Jaylen Hoard anota la canasta ganadora gala a pesar de la remontada de 19 puntos de los serbios
articles.body: Los Francia - Serbia van camino de convertirse en la nueva gran rivalidad del baloncesto europeo y casi mundial. Y no sólo porque se enfrenten dos escuadras de enorme calidad y que siempre tratan de llegar lo más lejos posible en los torneos que compiten. Tener a dos de los cinco mejores jugadores del planeta ayuda y mucho. Decía Nikola Jokic tras el primer amistoso: "Un amigo me dijo un día que no hay amistosos, sino partidos de preparación. Siempre he entendido que cualquier partido es importante y me gusta afrontarlos así". Para el serbio no hay partidos relajados, da igual lo que haya en juego. Y lo volvió a demostrar en Orleans. Francia ganó a Serbia, 91-90, en un choque en el que de nuevo el que iba ganando se relajó y tuvo que volver a ganar el partido al final, como en el primer partido, pero al revés. Los franceses llegaron a mandar hasta por 19 cuando al descanso el marcador lucía un 54-35. Si ya en cualquier partido remontar 19 puntos es complicado, en un amistoso parece misión casi imposible. Pero no cuando está Jokic jugando. El serbio lideró a su país para que se metiera en el partido y luego los triples de Jovic y Dobric hicieron el resto. Serbia fue acortando poco a poco su desventaja con un parcial de 4-18 hasta ponerse por delante, 72-76 a falta de 6:48. Fueron entonces los franceses los que reaccionaron para volver a controlar el choque. Con Sylvain Francisco dirigiendo y Luwawu-Cabarrot anotando, Francia volvió a irse, 85-77, y ya parecía algo definitivo. Pero no, los balcánicos volvieron al partido y a cinco segundos para el final se colocaron por delante, 89-90 con una canasta de Guduric. La canasta final de Jaylen Hoard sobre la bocina en un error defensivo serbio, dio la victoria a Francia. Lo celebraron como un triunfo oficial. En Francia Francisco fue el mejor anotador con 20 puntos, mientras que Luwawu-Cabarrot hizo 19 y Wembanyama aportó 18 y cinco rebotes en 24 minutos. Jokic volvió a dar otro recital con 34 puntos, 13 rebotes y cinco asistencias jugando casi 30 minutos para 34 de valoración. Jovic anotó 13 puntos y Guduric, 11. El de Orleans ha sido el último partido de preparación de ambas selecciones. Ya en las Ventanas, Francia jugará contra Eslovenia (27 de agosto) y Suecia (30), con la tranquilidad que da su 5-1 en el grupo L, mientras que Serbia lo hará ante Islandia (28) e Italia (31), algo más apurado por el 4-2 que lucen.

The Miami Heat signed veteran sharpshooter Klay Thompson on a reported 2-year, $11.5 million deal after receiving a contract buyout from the Dallas Mavericks, per Sam Amick and Darnell Mayberry of The Athletic.

Thompson took nearly a $10 million discount to join Miami, giving the team added flexibility to build the rest of their roster:

Here's a look at Miami's updated roster following the move.

Thompson established himself as one of the best shooters in NBA history during his tenure with the Golden State Warriors from 2011-24, earning five All-Star nods and two All-NBA selections.

He currently ranks No. 4 on the league's all-time three-point shooting list .

His Warriors career was interrupted by Achilles and knee injuries that caused him to miss two straight seasons from 2019-21.

Still, Thompson returned to Golden State and helped the organization remain successful before signing a three-year contract with the Mavericks as a free agent in July 2024.

At the time, Dallas was coming off an NBA Finals appearance led by star Luka Dončić. The Mavericks ultimately traded Dončić to the Los Angeles Lakers during the 2024-25 season, though.

Thompson averaged 12.9 points, 2.8 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game while shooting 40.3 percent from the field and 38.7 percent from behind the arc throughout his time in Dallas.

He'll now look to space the floor for Bam Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo in Miami after the Heat acquired the latter star in a blockbuster trade with the Milwaukee Bucks on June 22.

articles.title: España aplasta a Bélgica en una prueba de mucho valor
articles.standfirst: El partido deja claro que el trabajo de Méndez y la selección va por muy buen camino
articles.summary: El partido deja claro que el trabajo de Méndez y la selección va por muy buen camino
articles.body: Una cosa ha quedado clara en Tenerife: jugando a este nivel, el demostrado ante Bélgica, España puede aspirar a cualquier cosa. 'Volvamos a soñar' es el lema de la gira de la selección y el equipo está dando los pasos para poder soñar de verdad. La selección aplastó a Bélgica, 95-67 en el tercer partido del torneo Internacional de Tenerife. Es cierto que esto es un partido de preparación y las conclusiones deben ser sacadas con perspectiva, pero ante las campeonas de Europa se vio un equipo que cada vez avanza más hacia la idea que su seleccionador quiere. Una defensa casi impenetrable que dispara luego un ataque eléctrico y muy eficiente. España llevaba cuatro derrotas seguidas ante Bélgica incluyendo dos finales de Europeos. Ganar este partido puede ser crucial si en algún momento ambos equipos cruzan sus caminos en el Mundial, que puede ocurrir. Las belgas ya saben lo que esta selección española puede dar. La puesta en escena del equipo de Méndez fue formidable. Por un lado el ataque funcionó a la perfección, y no sólo los tiros, sino también las penetraciones o los contraataques culmindos tras robo. Y todo eso con una enorme defensa que desactivó a Meeseman, su principal referente. Ya en el primer cuarto se vieron las intenciones españolas con el 25-16 al final del periodo. El despertar de Meeseman acercó a Bélgica, 33-31, pero los triples de Helena Pueyo volvieron a disparar a la selección. Al descanso, 45-42 por los siete puntos encajadas en los últimos instantes. Pero en la reanudación, las de Méndez seguían de subida y fueron disparando la ventaja. Los triples siguieron cayendo (13 anotó España de 25 intentos), demostando que si están acertadas desde el arco, es un equipo muy difícil de ganar. Una muestra del acierto español fueron los 5/8 de Pueyo, el 2/3 de Maite Cazorla y, sobre todo, el 4/4 de Elena Buenavida. La ventaja se disparó hasta los 30 puntos y una máxima de 33, 91-58, para acabar con el +28 final que quizá no da la imagen real entre ambos equipos, pero que pone de manifiesto dónde está España ahora mismo. Las últimas dos pruebas de la selección serán en Zaragoza ante Mali y China. Luego, ya pueden soñar con el Mundial. Iyana Martín acabó con 15 puntos y 8 asistencias, Pueyo también hizo 15 puntos, Cazorla aportó 14 y seis asistencias y Buenavida e Irati Etxarri firmaron 12. En Bélgica, Lisowa fue la mejor con 12 y Meeseman se quedó en 10.

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

According to The Athletic's Sam Amick and Darnell Mayberry , the veteran signed a two-year, $11.5 million contract with the Heat after reaching a buyout with the Mavs.

After clearing waivers on Sunday, he was able to officially sign with Miami.

The deal reportedly includes a player option for the second year and also includes a 15 percent trade kicker.

The Mavericks announced Friday that they are buying out the final year of Klay Thompson's contract. The five-time All-Star was due to earn $17.5 million for the 2026-27 season

Dallas' move is a sign of how far Thompson's value has diminished around the NBA. Once one of the best two-way players in the league, he fell out of the Mavericks' starting rotation midway through last year.

In 69 appearances, he averaged 11.7 points and set career lows in overall field-goal percentage (39.3) and three-point percentage (38.3).

Jason Kidd shifted Thompson to the bench after seven games, which made for a delicate situation considering Dallas promised him a starting spot when it made its pitch during the 2024 offseason.

Kidd indicated it was only a temporary tactical change, and the 36-year-old was with the first unit again in a loss to the New York Knicks in mid-November. But he eventually assumed a reserve role again.

The Warriors saw the writing on the wall with a player who had become a franchise icon.

Head coach Steve Kerr and general manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. were pragmatic rather than sentimental with Thompson's usage during the 2023-24 season and then regarding how they approached his subsequent free agency.

Breaking up the "Splash Brothers" wasn't a move anybody in the Bay Area wanted to make, but the Warriors understood Thompson was on a downward trajectory. Missing two full seasons because of a torn ACL and a torn Achilles accelerated the inevitable decline that was coming as he got older.

A change of scenery and a desire to prove Golden State wrong didn't spark a renaissance in his first year with Dallas. He averaged 14 points per game, his lowest output since his rookie season, and his field-goal percentage (41.2) was a personal worst at the time.

The Mavs knew they weren't getting Thompson at his peak when they signed him. They presumably envisioned him occupying a role similar to Ray Allen during his two-year run with the Miami Heat and toward the end of his Boston Celtics tenure. Allen remained a capable three-point specialist as his career wound down, shooting 37.5 percent from beyond the arc in his final season.

Thompson's long-range prowess has even started to desert him, though, which makes the other flaws in his game tougher to ignore. He's not as dogged a defender and he can't score off the dribble like he once did.

The days of Thompson being a big difference-maker on a contender may be over, but he's a low-risk addition for a Heat team that saw Giannis Antetokounmpo enter the fold this summer.

articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom Ejected from Fever-Sky Game After He Was Confronted by Sky's Cloud

articles.title: Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham's Final Box Score Stats, Highlights as Fever Beat Sky
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever's short losing streak is over.
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever's short losing streak is over.

Indiana ended its two-game losing streak and improved to 25-14 on the season with a 113-90 victory over the Chicago Sky on Sunday. Caitlin Clark and the Fever entered the contest as 3.5-point favorites on FanDuel Sportsbook and finished the season sweep of Chicago even though Aliyah Boston was sidelined with a lower leg injury.

Clark and Kelsey Mitchell continued their season-long brilliance with 14 combined three-pointers, while Sophie Cunningham added three points off the bench. Natasha Cloud led the way for Chicago in a losing effort, but there was only so much she could do to counter Clark making more history:

Indiana entered the game on a poorly timed mini-slide that knocked it into fifth place in the standings that have just a handful of games separating the second seed from the eighth seed. The standings flip with seemingly every result, so Sunday was an important opportunity to bounce back against an opponent they have controlled play against this season.

Yet Chicago was ready to put up a fight in the early going.

The home team used a balanced attack to seize a 51-50 halftime advantage with eight different players scoring at least four points before intermission. The Sky's bench provided a much-needed boost, which helped counter Clark dominating play on an individual level with her combination of outside shooting and facilitating when defenders collapsed.

Makayla Timpson also got off to a quick start for Indiana, which helped make up for the loss of Boston. Clark even found her on a behind-the-back pass, although the visitors still found themselves behind early due to their defensive issues without their frontcourt star.

Still, offensive dominance is often enough to overcome defensive woes on the other side, as Clark and Mitchell reminded the Sky in the third quarter.

The duo of backcourt stars took over with an array of deep threes, floaters and drives into the lane, and Chicago had no answer. Frankly, there may be no team in the entire league that will have a counter for the guards when they are both playing at their best, although the Sky were still well within striking distance heading to the fourth thanks in part to an offensive flurry from Cloud.

But there would be no fourth-quarter rally for Chicago.

The Clark and Mitchell show led the way, but the Fever finally dialed up the defensive intensity when the game was on the line as well. The Sky failed to generate any offensive momentum until it was too late, and it would have required quite the offensive performance to overcome the two Indiana guards.

With Sunday's win secured, the Fever will now look to start a winning streak and climb the standings as they host the Connecticut Sun on Friday.

articles.body:
The Washington Mystics earned their first WNBA playoff berth since 2023 with Sunday's win over the Portland Fire paired with a loss from the Chicago Sky.

Washington is on pace to secure the No. 7 seed, sitting at 22-15.

No Cunningham-Carrington Issues in Rematch (AP)

2. Golden State Valkyries (25-11); clinched

11. Los Angeles Sparks (13-24); eliminated

The Mystics lost 28 games and finished seven back of the eighth-place Golden State Valkyries in 2025. The general vibes around the organization were not those of a team that was well outside of the postseason hunt, though.

That's because Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen both made the All-Star team as rookies, and the 2026 WNBA draft promised to bring more reinforcements for a young core.

Citron is averaging more points (16.9) and assists (4.1) than she did last year, and Iriafen has seen a bump to her scoring (15.1) and rebounds (9.3). Both are taking steps forward in their development.

Shakira Austin, meanwhile, has expanded her offensive repertoire. Seventeed made three-pointers may not seem like a lot, but they are for a player who knocked down three total threes through her first four seasons.

Depth behind the starting rotation has come from 2026 first-rounders Lauren Betts and Cotie McMahon. Georgia Amoore, who missed her entire rookie campaign through injury, is second on the team in assists (3.5).

Ironically, the 25-year-old Amoore is one of the oldest players.

Washington is bucking almost every historic precedent. Teams with rosters this young have by and large been very, very bad.

Even when accounting for the fact the WNBA has diluted the talent pool a bit through expansion, putting together a winning record when only three players on the roster have more than one year of service time is incredible.

For right now, the Mystics are playing with house money because they're ahead of schedule in their rebuild. Winning a series would be nice, but simply having Citron, Iriafen, Betts and McMahon taste playoff basketball is important in its own right.

The postseason could also be instructive to the coaching staff and front office toward how to continue building around Citron and Iriafen.

articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom ejected from WNBA game after being confronted by Sky’s Natasha Cloud
articles.summary: The WNBA has been the subject of recent debates about whether transgender women should be allowed to play in the league. There has never been such a player in the WNBA.
articles.body: CHICAGO — Former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from Sunday night’s Indiana-Chicago WNBA game after he was confronted by Sky guard Natasha Cloud late in the third quarter. Freedom was sitting along the baseline. He had on a black shirt that read “WOMAN noun. adult human female.” The Fever called for a timeout after Cloud scored inside with 1:22 left in the third. Cloud then did a chest bump with teammate Aicha Coulibaly before turning around and walking in Kanter’s direction. Cloud, 34, started yelling and pointing at Kanter, also 34, as she approached him. A standing Kanter held his arms out and took one step on the court as security and a handful of Sky players moved in between the two. “There was just a fan incident and the security handled it, and we’re just going to focus on the game,” Chicago forward Azura Stevens said after the Sky’s 113-90 loss. Chicago coach Tyler Marsh said Cloud was concerned about being a distraction for the team. “I told her she wasn’t,” Marsh said. “I told her that we all embrace her as someone that protects our team and protects people that need to be protected and so Tash is always going to stand on that, and we stand for Tash.” Freedom stopped near the basket to plead his case to security as he was escorted from the court area. He spun around while holding his shirt out and encouraged the crowd to respond as he walked toward the front lobby. He had a conversation with a group of police officers before departing Wintrust Arena. “I didn’t see it. We were talking about the next play in our huddle,” Indiana star Caitlin Clark said. “So I think that’s probably a question for Chicago.” Cloud met with team and league security after the game. She did not speak with the media. The WNBA has been the subject of recent debates on whether transgender women — people assigned male at birth who transition to align with their gender identity — should be allowed to participate in the league. There has never been such a player in the WNBA. Although the league’s collective bargaining agreement says the WNBA is restricted to women, it contains no more specific language about gender identity or sex assigned at birth. Fever guard Sophie Cunningham said in an ESPN profile published last month that she was opposed to transgender girls and women competing in girls’ and women’s sports. Freedom and Royce White, another former NBA player, have declared themselves eligible for the WNBA draft, saying they identify as women. Kanter joined a small rally in support of Cunningham outside the arena before the game. Asked if he had a message for Kanter, Marsh praised the league and its players. “If you come to a game you should probably come to enjoy the basketball,” he said, “and that seems pretty simple to me. I think these players deserve that and have earned that. Being a former basketball player, you should probably understand and feel that too.”

articles.title: El nuevo Real Madrid se estrenará en la SuperCup de la Euroliga
articles.standfirst: La competición se disputará en Abu Dabi los días 18 y 19 de septiembre
articles.summary: La competición se disputará en Abu Dabi los días 18 y 19 de septiembre
articles.body: La Euroliga anunció este lunes el nacimiento de una nueva competición. Ya se habló de ello en julio, aunque no hubo anuncio oficial. Pero la nueva SuperCup ya ha recibido la luz verde y por lo tanto habrá un nuevo título que sumar a la lista de los objetivos de esta temporada. La SuperCup que se celebrará en Abu Dabi los próximos 18 y 19 de septiembre reúne un cartel de lujo: Olympiacos, Real Madrid, Fenerbahce y Dubai Basketball. Los griegos acuden por su condición de actuales campeones de la Euroliga, el Madrid por ser finalista, los turcos por ser el anterior campeón y el Dubai como equipo anfitrión. Es cierto que, como ocurre con otras 'supercopas' se trata de un torneo entre la pretemporada y el inicio oficial de la competición, pero no deja de ser un título y sobre todo con un cartel tan atractivo como el que ofrece en este caso la SuperCup. El Madrid, muy renovado, podrá poner a prueba su proyecto a las primeras de cambio contra equipos que, en mayo, estén peleando por entrar en la Final Four que, en principio, también se celebrará en Abu Dabi. El equipo de Pedro Martínez cuenta con numerosas novedades en su plantilla: el propio entrenador, Jaime Pradilla, Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot, Mikael Jantunen, Max Shulga, Olivier Sarr y Eli Ndiaye a falta de que Damian Jones sea presentado y quizá a la llegada de un dos, aunque este podría llegar en los descartes de la NBA. El Madrid ya habrá jugado partidos de preparación ya que participará en el torneo Costa del Sol de Málaga junto a La Laguna Tenerife y Unicaja, pero no jugará la Supercopa Endesa en Badalona, que, por cierto, coincide en fechas con la europea (19 y 20). Disputar dos partidos ante equipos punteros de la Euroliga es una excelente puesta a punto para los de Martínez. Además, se da la circunstancia de que los blancos debutarán en la Euroliga precisamente en Dubái el próximo 24 de septiembre, cinco días después de jugar la SuperCup, por lo que podrán quedarse en Dubai para disputar el partido ya oficial de Liga regular. En el torneo de la Euroliga se podrán ver también algunas novedades en equipos muy favoritos como el Olympiacos: Jean Montero o Codi Miller-McIntyre, Fenerbahce: Sertac Sanli, Shavon Shields, Trent Forrest, Braxton Key, Shane Larkin o Will Clyburn, o el Dubai con el estreno de Xavi Pascual y las llegadas de Tornike Shengelia, Mamadi Diakite, Jaron Blossomgame o Elie Okobo. El formato de la SuperCup será igual que el de una Final Four. El viernes 18 se disputarán las semifinales con el Olympiacos - Fenerbahce a las 16.00 hora peninsular (18.00 hora local), y el Real Madrid - Dubai Basketball a las 19.00 en España (21.00 en Abu Dabi). El sábado habrá un tercer y cuarto puesto (16.00 en España) y la final tres horas después (19.00). "La SuperCup refleja nuestra ambición de seguir innovando y ampliando el alcance del baloncesto de clubes europeo", valoró el CEO de la Euroliga Chus Bueno. "Lanzar esta nueva competición en Abu Dabi nos permite conectar con nuevas audiencias y, al mismo tiempo, ofrecer a aficionados, clubes y socios un evento de primer nivel que exhibe lo mejor de nuestro deporte. Esperamos consolidar la SuperCup como una cita destacada en el calendario internacional de baloncesto".

articles.title: Enes Kanter provoca su expulsión en un partido de la WNBA
articles.standfirst: El turco se enzarzó en una discusión con Natasha Cloud y luego publicó varios mensajes
articles.summary: El turco se enzarzó en una discusión con Natasha Cloud y luego publicó varios mensajes
articles.body: La polémica que estalló con el anuncio de Enes Kanter de presentarse al Draft de la WNBA de 2027 porque "me siento mujer", alimentada por otro ex NBA como Royce White, no sólo está muy lejos de acabar, sino que es alimentada a lo bestia día a día. El último capítulo tuvo lugar en un Chicago Sky ante Indiana Fever y lo protagonizó el propio ex jugador turco, con un mensaje en su camiseta, una publicación en el descanso y un final abrupto que supuso su expulsión del Wintrust Arena de Chicago. Kanter se presentó en el partido con una camiseta en la que se podía leer: "Mujer. Sustantivo. Ser humano adulto femenino". El turco sigue manteniendo que en las normas de la WNBA se indica que sólo las mujeres pueden jugar en su competición. Pero según el polémico ex jugador, no hay una definición concreta del término mujer. Y mantiene que si él se siente mujer, puede jugar en la Liga. Otra de las provocaciones de Kanter llegó en el descanso. Publicó en redes un mensaje en el que ponía: "Es medio tiempo y mecesito usar el lavabo. Las reglas son las reglas", acompañado de una foto en la que se le veía en el lavabo de las mujeres. Finalmente llegó su expulsión. Natasha Cloud, jugadora de las Sky, le fue a buscar a la pie de pista, donde estaba Kanter, y se enzarzó con él en una discusión que el turco, claro, no sólo no rehuyó, sino que elevó a lo máximo. Finalmente Kanter, se ve en la imagen, fue invitado a abandonar el pabellón y lo hizo pidiendo más ruido al público y mostrando ostensiblemente el mensaje que llevaba en su camiseta. Poco después Kanter publicó un nuevo mensaje en las redes: ¡Acabo de ser expulsado de un partido de la WNBA por apoyar a las MUJERES! Que eso cale hondo, ¡AMÉRICA!. Antes había publicado otro: "Siempre son mujeres criticando a otras mujeres".  Es un capítulo más de una polémica que está a años luz de resolverse. Al menos de momento. Y lo que está ocurriendo con Kanter y la WNBA en realidad es un resumen de una sociedad dividida entre los partidarios de que los deportistas trans puedan participar en competiciones de mujeres y los que no. Y el debate seguirá.
